articles.title: Historic St Michael's Mount cannons airlifted for restoration
articles.summary: Cannons are lifted from St Michael's Mount by helicopter so they can be taken away for restoration.
articles.body:
When 300-year-old cannons at St Michael's Mount in Cornwall needed to be restored, the Royal Navy stepped in.

The cannons could only be taken off the island by helicopter, and a Merlin Mk2 helicopter from Atlantic Flight 814 Naval Air Squadron lifted each cannon individually off the island.

The operation was planned by the crew based at the Royal Naval Air Station at RNAS Culdrose, near Helston, in Cornwall.

Years of exposure to salt spray contributed to corrosion of the cannons - which will be treated at Dorothea Restorations in Bristol.

articles.title: What's going on between Kelly Clarkson and a Brooklyn store bird?
articles.summary: The Since U Been Gone singer claims she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" an item in the store.
articles.body:
A boutique store called Art of Play in Brooklyn has found itself at the centre of a social media storm, after Grammy winner Kelly Clarkson complained that they would not let her buy a singing and dancing mechanical bird that was on the wall.

The Since U Been Gone singer claimed she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird - which she said had a price tag of $15,000 (£11,000).

Art of Play has defended how it treated the star, saying the wooden bird is permanently attached to the wall and is not for sale.

It said that during Clarkson's five-minute visit on Saturday, an employee suggested to her that she could buy an identical bird for $15,000.

articles.title: Motociclista age rápido e salva frentista de engasgo no Ceará; vídeo | G1
articles.standfirst: Valdi Neto, de 26 anos, aprendeu a Manobra de Heimlich através de um vídeo na internet e foi a primeira vez que usou para desengasgar alguém.
articles.summary: Valdi Neto, de 26 anos, aprendeu a Manobra de Heimlich através de um vídeo na internet e foi a primeira vez que usou para desengasgar alguém.
articles.body:
Um motociclista de aplicativo salvou um frentista que estava engasgado com um pedaço de carne em um posto de combustíveis em Sobral , no interior do Ceará. O caso ocorreu na noite da última terça-feira (13) e foi registrado pela câmera de segurança do estabelecimento. (Assista ao vídeo acima.)

Segundo Valdi Neto, de 26 anos , ele havia deixado um passageiro próximo ao posto de combustíveis e, quando se aproximou do local, viu o frentista tentando fazer a Manobra de Heimlich no colega de trabalho.

"Inicialmente eu pensei que fosse brincadeira entre eles, mas quando fui um pouco mais à frente, vi que ele realmente estava se engasgando. Então decidi parar lá para ajudar", falou Valni Neto.

Ainda conforme o motociclista, o homem já estava engasgado a quase um minuto quando ele iniciou o procedimento.

"Ele já estava pálido. Teve um momento que a gente quase cai, porque ele pesou para o lado, já estava ficando insconsciente. Só pensei:'Deus, é você e eu'. E graças a Deus deu tudo certo", disse o motociclista.

Aprendeu manobra de desengasgo na internet

Frentista é salvo por motociclista após se engasgar com pedaço de carne em Sobral. — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda de acordo com Valdi Neto, ele aprendeu a Manobra de Heimlich em um vídeo na internet e foi a primeira vez que ele precisou aplicá-la para ajudar alguém.

"Nunca tinha feito essa manobra, só tinha visto um vídeo na internet para caso um dia eu precisasse, para ter essa noção, e só fiz uma aula de primeiros socorros no Ensino Médio, em 2016. Na hora eu pensava: 'se eu não consegui, o que vou fazer'", relatou Valdi, ao g1 .

Para o motociclista, foi Deus quem fez ele pegar a corrida próximo ao posto e ter a oportunidade de ajudar o frentista.

"Eu já estava indo para casa, já ia desligar o aplicativo, quando tocou essa corrida para eu voltar. É porque realmente eu tinha que estar lá naquele momento, para ajudar o rapaz", falou o motociclista.

articles.title: Carreta com mármore tomba, motorista fica ferido e poste cai no ES | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu no distrito de Conduru, entre Castelo e Cachoeiro de Itapemirim; poste de internet foi arrancado e atingiu outro caminhão na pista
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu no distrito de Conduru, entre Castelo e Cachoeiro de Itapemirim; poste de internet foi arrancado e atingiu outro caminhão na pista
articles.body:
Uma carreta carregada com 60 chapas de mármore tombou nesta quarta-feira (14) na ES-166, no distrito de Conduru, entre Castelo e Cachoeiro de Itapemirim, no Sul do Espírito Santo. O motorista ficou ferido e foi levado para um hospital de Castelo.

Com o acidente, um poste de telefonia e internet foi arrancado e caiu sobre outro caminhão que passava pelo local. O segundo motorista não se feriu.

De acordo com relatos de amigos do condutor que estiveram no local, uma das rodas da carreta teria travado, fazendo com que ele perdesse o controle da direção e tombasse às margens da rodovia.

O motorista, natural de Sergipe, havia saído de Castelo e seguia viagem de volta para o estado nordestino. A previsão era fazer paradas em Cachoeiro de Itapemirim e Colatina para complementar a carga.

As chapas de mármore ficaram espalhadas pelo canteiro lateral da rodovia. A estimativa inicial é de que o prejuízo com a perda do material ultrapasse R$ 60 mil.

O acidente também danificou a rede de telefonia e internet. Equipes da Polícia Militar foram acionadas para orientar o trânsito, que funcionou temporariamente em meia pista e provocou retenções.

Funcionários responsáveis pela rede de cabeamento foram mobilizados para fazer os reparos. A remoção da carreta e a limpeza do local dependiam da chegada da seguradora.

O trânsito na ES-166 foi normalizado e liberado nos dois sentidos.

* Texto adaptado por Patrick Mizrahi, aluno do 29º Curso de Residência em Jornalismo. Este conteúdo teve orientação e edição de Juirana Nobres.

articles.title: Fundo de Quintal, Dionne Warwick, baile charme: o que fazer no Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação entre os dias 15 e 21 de outubro reúne shows, teatro, exposições e atividades para crianças.
articles.summary: Programação entre os dias 15 e 21 de outubro reúne shows, teatro, exposições e atividades para crianças.
articles.body:
A programação cultural do Rio tem entre seus destaques uma grande homenagem ao grupo Fundo de Quintal, domingo (18), na Cidade do Samba, com direito a convidados como Zeca Pagodinho e Péricles.

No sábado (17), o Vivo Rio recebe uma apresentação da turnê de despedida da cantora Dionne Warwick, vencedora de seis prêmios Grammy.

Também no sábado, o projeto Rio Cheio de Charme leva a tradicional experiência do Baile do Viaduto de Madureira para o Parque Garota de Ipanema, no Arpoador.

Veja abaixo os eventos e monte seu roteiro:

A cantora Andrea Ferrer apresenta o espetáculo intimista "Viver a Vida Só de Amor" quinta-feira (15), no Teatro Cândido Mendes. Em uma homenagem afetiva a Roberto Carlos, a artista baiana revisita canções compostas e imortalizadas pelo Rei sob uma nova perspectiva feminina e pessoal. Acompanhada por Misael da Hora no piano e Stanley Netto nos sopros, Andrea traz ao palco sucessos e músicas marcantes de diferentes gerações, como "Olha", "O Progresso" e "Nossa Senhora".

🗓️ Quando? Quinta-feira (15), às 20h📍 Onde? Teatro Cândido Mendes - Rua Joana Angélica, 63, Ipanema💲 Quanto? Entre R$ 40 e R$ 80 no Sympla.

Cantora norte-americana Dionne Warwick — Foto: Dionne Warwick/Divulgação

A seis vezes vencedora do Grammy, Dionne Warwick, traz ao Rio de Janeiro a sua turnê de despedida dos palcos, "Over and Out – A Farewell Tour". O show histórico, que acontece no sábado (17), celebra a trajetória de uma das artistas mais influentes da música mundial, recém-incluída no Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, e promete emocionar o público com um repertório repleto de clássicos imortais, como “I Say a Little Prayer” e “That’s What Friends Are For”.

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (17), às 20h30 (abertura da casa 2h antes). 📍 Onde? Vivo Rio - Avenida Infante Dom Henrique, 85, Parque do Flamengo. 💲 Quanto? a partir de - R$440,00 (meia-entrada) l R$880 (inteira).

George Israel e o DJ Leo Paes Leme tocam na Rockeria — Foto: Divulgação

A festa Rockeria celebra 14 anos com show de George Israel no formato “Baile do George”, em que o músico revisita canções de sua trajetória e sucessos do rock nacional e internacional. No repertório, entram músicas do Kid Abelha, Cazuza, Paralamas do Sucesso e outros artistas.

A noite também terá sets dos DJs Leo Paes Leme e Gui Scarpa , com faixas de diferentes vertentes do rock.

“É uma festa que adoro e que tem uma relação muito forte com a música e a noite carioca. Vai ser uma noite para cantar, dançar e celebrar a música”, diz George.

Quando? Sábado (17), às 21h. Onde? Clube dos Macacos - Rua Pacheco Leão, 2038, Horto. Quanto? R$ 60 (2º lote) e R$ 70 (3º lote). Classificação: não informada.

No sábado (17), a música pernambucana invade o Rio de Janeiro com os shows de Mestre Ambrósio e Banda Eddie. Celebrando os 30 anos de seu primeiro álbum, um marco do movimento manguebeat, a banda Mestre Ambrósio retorna aos palcos com sua formação original. A noite conta ainda com a Banda Eddie lançando seu novo disco, "Noturna", e a DJ Sthael animando a pista com ritmos do Norte e Nordeste nos intervalos.

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (17), a partir das 20h (abertura dos portões)📍 Onde? Circo Voador - Rua dos Arcos, s/n, Lapa💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 80 (meia-entrada) e R$ 160 (inteira).

O projeto Rio Cheio de Charme leva a tradicional experiência do Baile do Viaduto de Madureira para a Zona Sul carioca no sábado (17). Com a proposta de conectar territórios e celebrar a cultura negra e suburbana do Rio de Janeiro, o evento ao ar livre reúne DJs residentes, dançarinos e tem como grande atração o lendário Corello DJ, um dos criadores do movimento e responsável por cunhar o termo "charme" no país. A festa promete resgatar a memória afetiva de diferentes gerações com muito R&B e os clássicos passos de dança coletivos.

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (17), das 16h às 22h📍 Onde? Parque Garota de Ipanema - Avenida Francisco Bhering, 2-224, Arpoador💲 Quanto? Entrada franca.

Em outubro, a série Música no Museu promove concertos gratuitos em diversos espaços culturais e históricos do Rio de Janeiro. Com o objetivo de democratizar a música de concerto e aproximar o público de grandes intérpretes e compositores, o projeto apresenta recitais de piano, violão e canto coral com repertórios que passeiam por clássicos brasileiros e internacionais. As apresentações desta etapa acontecem nos dias 21, 22, 27, 28 e 31 de outubro, passando por locais icônicos da cidade.

🗓️ Quando? Dias 21, 22, 27, 28 e 31 de outubro, em horários variados (12h30 ou 18h, dependendo do dia e local)📍 Onde? Diversos espaços: CCBB Rio (Centro), Centro Cultural Justiça Federal (Centro), Museu do Exército no Forte de Copacabana (Copacabana) e Palácio São Clemente / Consulado-Geral de Portugal (Botafogo).💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita.

Grupo Fundo de Quintal comemora 50 anos com evento especial na Cidade do Samba — Foto: Divulgação

No dia 18 de outubro, a Cidade do Samba recebe a edição especial do evento "Todo Mundo Canta Fundo" para celebrar os 50 anos de trajetória do icônico grupo Fundo de Quintal. O evento exalta o legado do conjunto nascido no Cacique de Ramos, responsável por introduzir instrumentos como o tantã e o banjo no gênero, e traz um show histórico repleto de clássicos como "O Show Tem Que Continuar" e "A Amizade". A grande festa contará com as participações especiais de Zeca Pagodinho, Gloria Groove e Péricles, além da roda de samba Terreiro de Crioulo na abertura e do grupo Fruta do Pé no encerramento.

🗓️ Quando? Domingo (18), a partir das 13h📍 Onde? Cidade do Samba Joãosinho Trinta - Rua Rivadávia Corrêa, 60, Gamboa💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 30 (vendas pelo Sympla).

A Unidos de Padre Miguel realiza mais uma edição de sua tradicional feijoada neste domingo (18 de outubro), reunindo a comunidade e os amantes do samba na Vila Vintém.

O evento, que embala os preparativos da agremiação para o Carnaval 2027, contará com a apresentação do cantor Lelê Carlos, o espetáculo dos segmentos da casa com o UPM Show e a presença da escola de samba convidada Paraíso do Tuiuti.

🗓️ Quando? Domingo (18 de outubro), a partir das 13h. 📍 Onde? Quadra da Unidos de Padre Miguel (Vila Vintém). 💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita. O prato de feijoada custa R$ 20 (mesas à venda no local; camarotes esgotados).

Para celebrar o seu quarto aniversário, a Arena Bangu recebe um show especial do grupo Sorriso Maroto no dia 18 de outubro. O evento festeja a trajetória do local com uma noite comemorativa dedicada aos maiores sucessos de um dos grupos mais populares do pagode nacional.

🗓️ Quando? Domingo (18), a partir das 17h📍 Onde? Arena Bangu, no Bangu Shopping - Rua Fonseca, 240, Bangu💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 100 (meia-entrada ou meia solidária mediante a doação de 1 kg de alimento não perecível). Vendas pelo Sympla ou na loja física no shopping (ao lado da Renner).

O espetáculo “Morra, Amor”, em cartaz até 29 de novembro, é um solo protagonizado por Mariana Santos, baseado no aclamado romance da escritora argentina Ariana Harwicz. A montagem acompanha a história de uma mulher isolada em uma casa de campo na França com o marido e o filho bebê, lidando com a sufocante rotina doméstica, a claustrofobia da maternidade recente e a perda de sentido no casamento.

🗓️ Quando? Sextas e sábados, às 20h; domingos, às 18h (até 29 de novembro). 📍 Onde? Teatro TotalEnergies - Sala Adolpho Bloch (R. do Russel, 804 - Glória). 💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 25 (meia-entrada) e R$ 50 (inteira). 🧒 Classificação: 14 anos.

Emily Matte e Rick Yates fazem leitura dramatizada de 'Harrogate' — Foto: Divulgação

O projeto Dramaturgia em Leituras apresenta no dia 19 de outubro o texto “Harrogate”, um drama psicológico do autor inglês Al Smith. A leitura encenada reúne os atores Emily Matte e Rick Yates, que dão vida a quatro personagens em uma trama de tensão emocional e humor ácido, ambientada na cozinha de uma família de classe média alta em Londres, acompanhando os encontros de um executivo com uma garota de programa, sua filha adolescente e sua esposa.

🗓️ Quando? Segunda-feira (19), às 19h. 📍 Onde? Teatro TotalEnergies - Sala Adolpho Bloch (R. do Russel, 804 - Glória). 💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita (retirada de ingressos na bilheteria a partir de duas horas antes da apresentação). 🧒 Classificação: Não informada.

O musical inédito "PIAF – Eu não me arrependo", em cartaz até 01 de novembro, revive nos palcos a acidentada e genial trajetória da cantora francesa Édith Piaf. Protagonizada por Laila Garin, a superprodução conta com uma orquestra e 12 atores em cena para narrar a jornada da artista, desde a infância na pobreza até a consagração mundial, embalada por clássicos eternos como ‘La Vie en Rose’, ‘Hymne à l’Amour’ e ‘Non, Je Ne Regrette Rien’.

🗓️ Quando? Quintas e sextas, às 20h; sábados, às 17h; domingos, às 18h (até 01 de novembro). 📍 Onde? Teatro Riachuelo Rio (Rua do Passeio, 40 – Centro). 💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 50 (balcão) até R$ 300 (plateia VIP, dependendo do dia). 🧒 Classificação: 12 anos.

O espetáculo “Uma Saudação às Divas” chega ao Rio de Janeiro no dia 21 de outubro para celebrar seus 10 anos de sucesso homenageando as maiores vozes femininas da música mundial. No palco, os cantores Claudia Nascimento, Amanda Orleans e Rafael Oliveira interpretam clássicos imortais de ícones como Whitney Houston, Aretha Franklin, Mariah Carey, Tina Turner, Beyoncé, Adele e Celine Dion.

🗓️ Quando? Quarta-feira (21 de outubro), às 20h. 📍 Onde? Teatro Riachuelo Rio (Rua do Passeio, 40 – Centro). 💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 50 (balcão) até R$ 240 (plateia VIP). 🧒 Classificação: Livre.

O espetáculo “Palavras de Mulher” imagina um encontro entre Clarice Lispector, Hilda Hilst, Carmen da Silva e Eneida de Moraes em uma “Biblioteca do Paraíso”, onde as escritoras compartilham memórias, ideias e reflexões sobre o universo feminino. Com texto de Rachel Gutiérrez e direção de Sergio Fonta, a montagem reúne figurinos de época, trilha sonora que vai de Debussy a Chiquinha Gonzaga e recursos de acessibilidade em todas as sessões.

🗓️ Quando? De 8 a 30 de outubro de 2026. Quintas e sextas, às 19h📍 Onde? Teatro Gláucio Gill — Praça Cardeal Arcoverde, s/n, Copacabana💲 Quanto? R$ 20 (meia) e R$ 40 (inteira)🧒 Classificação: 12 anos⏱️ Duração: 80 minutos

O Grupo Galpão retorna ao Teatro Carlos Gomes com o espetáculo "(Um) Ensaio Sobre a Cegueira", em curta temporada de 14 a 18 de outubro. A montagem é uma adaptação teatral do aclamado romance do escritor português José Saramago e acompanha uma sociedade atingida por uma misteriosa epidemia de cegueira. O conceito da peça propõe uma profunda reflexão sobre as relações humanas diante de situações-limite, levando ao palco temas como solidariedade, violência, poder e sobrevivência.

🗓️ Quando? De 14 a 18 de outubro. Quarta, quinta e sexta-feira, às 19h; sábado e domingo, às 17h📍 Onde? Teatro Carlos Gomes (Praça Tiradentes, 19, Centro)💲 Quanto? De R$ 45 a R$ 90🧒 Classificação: 16 anos.

O espetáculo de dança "Paragem" segue em cartaz no Sesc Copacabana até o dia 18 de outubro. Idealizada por Júlia Fernandez e Luna Leal, a montagem é um desdobramento do projeto Central Deriva e transforma em movimento os desafios de circular pelas cidades. O conceito da obra parte de experiências cotidianas nos transportes públicos — como caminhar, esperar e embarcar — para propor uma reflexão sobre mobilidade urbana, desigualdade e as barreiras de acessibilidade enfrentadas por diferentes corpos, contando com todas as sessões acessíveis em Libras e audiodescrição.

🗓️ Quando? Até 18 de outubro. Quintas e sextas, às 19h; sábados e domingos, às 17h📍 Onde? Multiuso do Sesc Copacabana (Rua Domingos Ferreira, 160, Copacabana)💲 Quanto? R$ 40 (inteira) e R$ 20 (meia-entrada), com valores promocionais para credenciados Sesc e gratuidade para público PCG🧒 Classificação: 14 anos.

Inspirado no clássico de Mary Shelley, “Frankinh@ – Uma História em Pedacinhos” conta a história de Victor Frankenstein, um jovem solitário que cria alguém para lhe fazer companhia, mas precisa aprender a conviver com as diferenças da criatura. Com direção de Camila Bauer, a peça combina teatro, ciência e ilusionismo e aborda temas como solidão, bullying, amizade e aceitação.

🗓️Quando? segunda (12), às 11h e 16h; temporada de 17 de outubro a 15 de novembro, sábados, às 15h, e domingos, às 11h e 16h / 📍Onde? CCBB Rio - Rua Primeiro de Março, 66 - Centro / 💲 Entrada: gratuita na estreia de 12 de outubro; na temporada, R$ 30 (inteira) e R$ 15 (meia), com ingressos pelo site do CCBB .

Obra de Suely Fahri presente na exposição 'As Palavras' — Foto: Paulo Rodrigues/Divulgação

A artista e poeta visual carioca Suely Farhi apresenta a exposição "As Palavras" no Centro Cultural Justiça Federal (CCJF), com visitação de 14 de outubro a 22 de novembro. Com curadoria de Luiza Interlenghi, a mostra reúne dez instalações criadas entre 1994 e os dias atuais, incluindo obras inéditas, totalmente dedicadas ao universo feminino. O conceito da exposição investiga o limiar entre palavra, imagem e espaço, utilizando intervenções textuais em objetos do cotidiano e projeções para iluminar a força da mulher, questionar tensões sociais e desenhar o invisível através da linguagem.

🗓️ Quando? De 14 de outubro a 22 de novembro. De terça a domingo, das 11h às 19h📍 Onde? Centro Cultural Justiça Federal - CCJF - Avenida Rio Branco, 241, Centro.💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita.

A exposição “Júlia Lopes de Almeida: Um Fenômeno Literário na Cena Carioca” homenageia a vida e a obra daquela que é considerada a maior romancista brasileira de sua época. Dividida em três núcleos, a mostra reúne fotografias, publicações e objetos pessoais da autora, destacando também sua atuação nas lutas abolicionista, feminista e ambiental. O projeto, que busca democratizar o acesso à memória cultural da cidade, segue em cartaz na Biblioteca Municipal José de Alencar, em Santa Teresa, até 28 de outubro. Em seguida, a itinerância chega à Biblioteca Municipal Marques Rebelo, na Tijuca, de 30 de outubro a 11 de novembro, contando também com oficinas e leituras dramatizadas ao longo da programação.

articles.title: Carreta tomba na Epia Sul e bloqueia pista no Núcleo Bandeirante | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente foi durante madrugada, na região do Núcleo Bandeirante, sentido Gama; motorista não precisou ser levado para hospital. Bloqueio da pista foi realizado para controlar vazamento de óleo. Trânsito foi desviado para marginal.
articles.summary: Carreta tomba na Epia Sul, no Núcleo Bandeirante, causando vazamento de óleo e desvio no trânsito para a via marginal nesta quinta-feira (15).
articles.body:
Uma carreta tombou na rodovia Epia Sul , na região do Núcleo Bandeirante , no Distrito Federal, durante a madrugada desta quinta-feira (15). Para conter o vazamento de óleo, um trecho da pista foi bloqueado, no sentido Gama, e o trânsito foi desviado para a via marginal (veja vídeo acima).

O motorista foi avaliado pelos bombeiros e estava consciente e orientado. Ele não precisou ser levado para um hospital.

Até as 7h50, o trecho da Epia Sul continuava bloqueado e o trânsito seguia lento na região. O Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem (DER) tenta retirar a carreta do local.

Carreta tomba e interdita trecho da Epia Sul — Foto: TV Globo

O acidente aconteceu por volta das 1h38. A TV Globo apurou que o motorista partiu de São Paulo e seguia em direção ao Aeroporto de Brasília , com uma carga e-commerce. Ao passar pela estação Estação Vargem Bonita, do BRT, o motorista perdeu o controle da direção. Ele invadiu o canteiro, derrubou uma árvore e tombou a carreta na pista contrária.

articles.title: Teresópolis começa a instalar semáforos inteligentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipamentos serão controlados pela Central de Monitoramento e terão tempos de sinal ajustados remotamente.
articles.summary: Equipamentos serão controlados pela Central de Monitoramento e terão tempos de sinal ajustados remotamente.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Teresópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, começou, nesta quarta-feira (14), a instalar novos semáforos inteligentes na cidade.

Os equipamentos serão integrados à Central de Monitoramento da Guarda Municipal, permitindo o controle remoto e ajustes nos tempos dos sinais.

O primeiro cruzamento a receber os novos equipamentos será o da Avenida Feliciano Sodré com a Rua Nova Friburgo. A substituição dos demais semáforos será feita gradativamente.

A mudança ocorre em meio às reclamações de motoristas e pedestres sobre o trânsito no município, especialmente após a implantação da faixa exclusiva de ônibus. Entre as principais queixas estão o tempo considerado insuficiente para a travessia de pedestres e a sensação de insegurança ao atravessar algumas vias.

A expectativa da Prefeitura é que a tecnologia ajude a reduzir as paradas e melhore a fluidez do trânsito, principalmente nos horários de maior movimento. Estudos técnicos citados pelo município apontam uma possibilidade de melhoria de até 60% no fluxo de veículos.

A modernização dos semáforos faz parte de um conjunto de mudanças viárias previstas para a cidade até dezembro. Entre elas está a criação de uma nova ligação entre a Rua Tenente Luiz Meireles e a Rua Nova Friburgo, com o objetivo de melhorar a circulação de veículos na região, especialmente nas ruas Tenente Luiz Meireles e Jornalista Delson Monteiro.

A previsão da Prefeitura é concluir a instalação dos novos semáforos em até 20 dias. O prazo, no entanto, pode sofrer alterações em função das condições climáticas.

articles.title: Ucrânia retoma ataques contra refinarias russas; 'Chega', diz Zelensky | G1
articles.standfirst: Instalação na região de Ryazan foi alvejada, segundo a Rússia. Kiev acusou Moscou de ignorar trégua parcial anunciada pelo presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. Zelensky disse ter se sentido traído pela compra de diesel russo pelos EUA e por interrupções na rede Starlink.
articles.summary: Instalação na região de Ryazan foi alvejada, segundo a Rússia. Kiev acusou Moscou de ignorar trégua parcial anunciada pelo presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. Zelensky disse ter se sentido traído pela compra de diesel russo pelos EUA e por interrupções na rede Starlink.
articles.body:
Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump e Volodymyr Zelensky. — Foto: Sputnik/Gavriil Grigorov/Pool via REUTERS, Reuters e Genya Savilov/AFP

A Ucrânia retomou nesta quinta-feira (15) seus ataques aéreos contra refinarias de petróleo russas, atingindo uma instalação na região de Ryazan, segundo o governador regional. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky , acusou a Rússia de não respeitar o cessar-fogo energético imposto por Donald Trump.

Kiev havia evitado atacar refinarias russas desde o anúncio de um cessar-fogo no setor energético entre Rússia e Ucrânia, feito no fim de semana pelo presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. Essa trégua, no entanto, parece ter pego ambos os países de surpresa.

Zelensky afirmou nesta quinta-feira em entrevista ao jornal britânico Financial Times que sua paciência com esse cenário se esgotou. “A restrição [aos ataques contra refinarias russas] acabou. Chega”, disse ele ao jornal.

Zelensky acusa a Rússia de ter ignorado a ordem de Trump e também vinha demonstrando crescente frustração com a continuidade dos bombardeios russos à infraestrutura energética ucraniana —ataques na quarta deixaram 600 mil pessoas sem energia na Ucrânia. Ele também acusou Moscou de intensificar seus ataques aéreos contra o país em meio a problemas técnicos na rede Starlink, que integra a defesa aérea ucraniana.

O presidente ucraniano já havia alertado anteriormente que a Ucrânia não suspenderia seus próprios ataques indefinidamente se a Rússia não fizesse o mesmo. Nesta quinta, ele voltou a criticar o que descreveu como favorecimento de Trump à Rússia com a compra de diesel russo , por exemplo.

Pavel Malkov, governador de Ryazan, afirmou em suas redes sociais que um grande ataque de drones ucranianos contra a região provocou um incêndio em uma refinaria de petróleo. “Os danos materiais estão sendo avaliados neste momento. Os serviços de emergência estão trabalhando no local”, disse.

O Kremlin afirmou que o ataque ucraniano desta quinta contradiz esforços de paz buscados pelos EUA.

Este é o segundo cessar-fogo energético entre Ucrânia e Rússia anunciado por Trump nos últimos anos, porém ambos ruíram rapidamente ou nem chegaram a ser postos em prática efetivamente pelos dois lados. O primeiro ocorreu em setembro.

Ucranianos em meio a destroços de casa atingida por bombardeio russo em Dnipro, na Ucrânia, em 15 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Stringer

Zelensky afirmou nesta quinta-feira que a Rússia fez um amplo ataque aéreo contra o território da Ucrânia durante a madrugada com mais de 850 drones Shahed. Os bombardeios atingiram a capital Kiev e outros 13 estados do país e "houve dezenas de impactos", segundo o líder ucraniano.

"É evidente que a Rússia escolheu deliberadamente intensificar seus ataques depois de obter um alívio nas sanções e de ver tentativas de pressionar a Ucrânia. A Rússia tira proveito de todas essas oportunidades e deve ser responsabilizada pelo que faz", afirmou.

O ataque russo deixou seis mortos , segundo autoridades ucranianas.

articles.title: Mega-Sena: Apostas da região ganham R$ 263,8 mil; prêmio acumula | G1
articles.standfirst: Prêmio principal acumulou em R$ 170 milhões.
articles.summary: A Mega-Sena acumulou em R$ 170 milhões após ninguém acertar as seis dezenas, mas um bolão e uma aposta simples da região garantiram prêmios na quina.
articles.body:
O prêmio principal da Mega-Sena acumulou mais uma vez e chegou à estimativa de R$ 170 milhões. No Vale do Paraíba e região, duas apostas bateram na trave, acertaram cinco dos seis números e faturaram, juntas, R$ 263,8 mil.

Elas foram registradas em Caraguatatuba , no Litoral Norte, e em Cachoeira Paulista . Em Caraguá, a aposta foi um bolão com 100 cotas, registrado na lotérica Bolão da Sorte. O prêmio total foi de R$ 211.071,00.

Já em Cachoeira Paulista, a aposta foi simples, com seis dezenas. Ela faturou um total de R$ 52.767,96 e foi registrada nos canais eletrônicos da Caixa.

Ninguém acertou os seis números e o prêmio principal da Mega-Sena agora está estimado em R$ 170 milhões. O próximo sorteio está previsto para o domingo (18), no Espaço da Sorte, em São Paulo.

Bilhete volante loteria megasena mega sena versão 2018 — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

As apostas podem ser feitas em qualquer lotérica do país ou pela internet, no site da Caixa Econômica Federal – acessível por celular, computador ou outros dispositivos.

É necessário fazer um cadastro, ser maior de idade (18 anos ou mais) e preencher o número do cartão de crédito.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para a aposta simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 15 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 22.522,50, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 10.003, ainda segundo a Caixa.

articles.title: Jovem desmaia em telhado e é resgatado pelos bombeiros em Bocaiuva | G1
articles.standfirst: Rapaz trabalhava em uma obra de um galpão quando passou mal. Ele foi retirado do telhado pelos bombeiros com apoio do Samu e encaminhado ao hospital para avaliação médica.
articles.summary: Rapaz trabalhava em uma obra de um galpão quando passou mal. Ele foi retirado do telhado pelos bombeiros com apoio do Samu e encaminhado ao hospital para avaliação médica.
articles.body:
Jovem fiu socorrido pelos bombeiros após desmaiar durante montagem de telhado — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

Um jovem de 23 anos foi socorrido pelo Corpo de Bombeiros após passar mal e desmaiar sobre o telhado de uma obra em Bocaiuva , nesta quarta-feira (14).

Segundo os bombeiros, a vítima trabalhava na montagem de um telhado de zinco em um galpão quando passou mal e desmaiou. Ele ficou sobre a estrutura, a uma altura de aproximadamente seis metros.

“Diante da situação, os bombeiros realizaram a imobilização adequada, utilizando técnicas de salvamento terrestre. Após imobilizar a vítima em uma maca skep, executaram a retirada da mesma do referido telhado até o solo”, informou a corporação.

O jovem não apresentava ferimentos e foi encaminhado ao hospital de Bocaiuva para avaliação médica. O resgate contou com o apoio de uma equipe do Samu.

articles.title: Vídeo mostra água quente saindo do chão em Caldas Novas | G1
articles.standfirst: Confeiteira Michelle Zebral chegou a tocar na água que saía de uma calçada em Caldas Novas. Segundo a prefeitura, vistoria técnica identificou que ocorrência decorreu de falha em tubulação do setor hoteleiro e já foi resolvida.
articles.summary: Vídeo mostra água quente e fumaça saindo de uma calçada em Caldas Novas. Prefeitura identificou vazamento em tubulação de água termal e informou que não havia mais vazamento.
articles.body:
Já imaginou encontrar água quente saindo do chão e soltando fumaça? Em Caldas Novas , na região sul de Goiás, a confeiteira Michelle Zebral registrou a situação inusitada no Setor Turista II. Em tom bem-humorado, ela filmou a água que brotava de uma área coberta por grama e terra e escorria para a rua, envolta em fumaça. A mulher chegou a tocar na água para mostrar a temperatura (veja o vídeo acima).

“Para quem nunca viu uma água quente brotando, olha isso. Olha a fumaça saindo aqui. A água tá simplesmente pegando fogo. Queimando. Vou pôr a mão pra vocês verem. Está muito quente, mas muito quente mesmo”, disse enquanto filmava.

Conhecida pelas fontes termais, a cidade teve o registro feito em 2 de outubro. Segundo a Prefeitura de Caldas Novas, o caso foi provocado por um vazamento em uma tubulação de distribuição de água termal, e não pelo surgimento de uma nova nascente.

A Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Semmarh) informou ao g1 que realizou uma verificação técnica no local e constatou que a ocorrência não se tratava de uma nascente nem de um afloramento natural de água termal (veja nota na íntegra no final da reportagem).

Água quente saindo do solo em Caldas Novas — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Michelle

Segundo a prefeitura, o Departamento Municipal de Água e Esgoto (Demae) vistoriou o local e descartou qualquer relação com a rede municipal de água tratada. O município ressaltou que a operação e a manutenção de tubulações de água termal não são atribuições do poder público.

Como o sistema de distribuição atende a diversos estabelecimentos da região, não foi possível identificar a empresa ou o condomínio responsável pela tubulação danificada.

Associação foi acionada para identificar a rede

A Semmarh comunicou a Associação das Empresas Mineradoras das Águas Termais de Goiás (Amat) para auxiliar na identificação da rede e na realização dos reparos necessários.

De acordo com a prefeitura, em nova vistoria realizada na quarta-feira (14), equipes da Semmarh e da Secretaria de Comunicação (Secom) constataram que não havia mais vazamento aparente no local.

O Governo de Caldas Novas esclarece que o vídeo divulgado nas redes sociais, mostrando água emergindo do solo no Setor Turista II, refere-se a uma ocorrência registrada há pelo menos uma semana, relacionada a um vazamento em uma tubulação do sistema de distribuição de águas termais.

A Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (SEMMARH) realizou uma verificação técnica no local e identificou que a ocorrência não se tratava de uma nascente ou de um afloramento natural de água termal, mas de um vazamento decorrente de falha na infraestrutura hidráulica.

O Departamento Municipal de Água e Esgoto (DEMAE) também esteve no local, com a finalidade específica de verificar eventual relação com a rede pública municipal de abastecimento de água tratada, hipótese que foi descartada.

Cabe esclarecer que a operação e a manutenção das tubulações destinadas à distribuição de águas termais não integram as atribuições operacionais do DEMAE. Dessa forma, a atuação dos órgãos municipais, neste caso, consistiu na verificação da ocorrência e na comunicação à entidade representativa do setor, respeitados os limites de suas competências legais.

Assim que tomou conhecimento da situação, a SEMMARH comunicou a Associação das Empresas Mineradoras das Águas Termais de Goiás (AMAT), entidade representativa das empresas que atuam no setor, para auxiliar na identificação da rede envolvida e no encaminhamento das providências técnicas cabíveis.

Ressalta-se que o sistema de distribuição de águas termais atende diferentes empreendimentos, não sendo possível, com base nas informações técnicas disponíveis, identificar a titularidade da tubulação ou atribuir responsabilidade pelo vazamento a um estabelecimento específico.

Nesta quarta-feira (14 de outubro), equipes da Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (SEMMARH) e da Secretaria Municipal de Comunicação (SECOM) realizaram uma nova verificação no local, constatando a ausência de vazamento aparente de água, conforme registros fotográficos realizados durante a visita.

Dessa forma, o Governo de Caldas Novas esclarece que as imagens divulgadas nas redes sociais retratam uma ocorrência anterior e não correspondem às condições verificadas atualmente no local.

O município reafirma seu compromisso com a transparência, a responsabilidade institucional e a prestação de informações técnicas precisas à população, atuando dentro de suas competências legais para o devido encaminhamento das situações identificadas.

articles.title: Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since 2023: report
articles.summary: At least 350 Palestinian children currently face ‘harsh conditions’ in Israeli prisons.
articles.body:
Israeli forces have detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since October 2023, the Palestinian Prisoner’s Society said.

In a report released on Wednesday, the Palestinian rights group said Israeli authorities continue to escalate their targeting of Palestinian children. At least 350 Palestinian children are currently facing “harsh conditions” in Israeli prisons.

On Tuesday, Israeli forces arrested at least six children from Hebron in the occupied West Bank, the report said.

The organisation said information regarding the number of children arrested in Gaza is unclear, given the thousands of missing persons in the besieged Gaza Strip, including children, and the ongoing policy of enforced disappearance.

The group said Israel’s policy of detention without charges or a release date constitutes “an additional violation and crime that leaves children facing the unknown and deprives them of family and educational stability”.

The report described Israeli practices that begin with “intimidation and arrest” and extend to “torture, starvation and denial of healthcare”.

The group highlighted the case of 15-year-old Mohammed Hamid, who contracted scabies, a contagious skin infestation, while he was detained in Ofer Prison, where rights groups have long documented abuses. He suffered severe infections, underwent heart surgery and was admitted to intensive care in critical condition. He subsequently had one of his legs amputated.

The organisation also highlighted the case of 17-year-old Walid Ahmed, who died in March 2025 after six months in Megiddo Prison. In December, an Israeli judge halted the investigation into his death, stating that although there was evidence of starvation, no definitive cause of death had been established.

Ahmed was imprisoned in Megiddo with his friend Mohammed Ibrahim , a teenager from Florida. Ibrahim was released after months of advocacy from US-based organisations and appeals from high-ranking lawmakers.

Mohammed Ibrahim was not the only young American held in Israeli prison without charge – Israeli forces reportedly took Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi from his West Bank home in a late-night raid in June. He turned 18 in detention, and authorities subsequently moved him from a youth holding area into an adult section at Ofer Prison.

Similarly, Israeli forces arrested 16-year-old Adam Wajeh Abdelfattah Karakrah, also an American, in July. Although he was set for release in August after his family secured bail, Israeli authorities abruptly reversed the decision to free him.

The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society called for “real international action” to ensure the release of arbitrarily detained children, enforce investigations and end torture, starvation and the denial of treatment in Israeli prisons.

Israeli forces have detained more than 25,000 Palestinians in the West Bank, and thousands more in Gaza, since Israel’s genocidal war began in October 2023.

articles.title: Seaton Carew little tern colony has worst breeding season
articles.summary: Planning is under way to improve the colony for the 2027 breeding season.
articles.body:
A little tern colony has experienced its toughest breeding season since establishing themselves at a site.

Since 2019 the seabirds have travelled about 3,000 miles (4,828km) from West Africa to Seaton Carew, near Hartlepool.

But this year the colony's 83 nesting pairs produced just 17 fledglings, compared to 67 in 2025.

Tees Valley Wildlife Trust said flooding and damage to the colony's perimeter fence contributed to difficult conditions for the birds.

The protective fencing around the nesting ground was washed away in high tides earlier this year.

Lead warden Derek Wood said a late arrival of their inshore food supply as well as predation also contributed to the birds' tough season.

In June, it was reported numbers were down 50%, which the team attributed to dogs being inside the exclusion zone.

"The season has been a difficult one for the dedicated wardens and volunteers who work tirelessly to protect the colony," Wood said.

But the team is hopeful the colony can bounce back when they return from Africa in spring, with plans to improve the site and further protect the birds under way.

Little Terns are currently classed as amber on the UK list of conservation concern.

articles.title: Restoring nature is key to a more resilient future
articles.summary: At COP17 and COP31, governments must accelerate positive tipping points in energy, food and finance.
articles.body:
Nature is humanity’s life-support system, but it is being depleted at an alarming rate, leaving our world increasingly vulnerable. From deadly heatwaves and raging wildfires to catastrophic floods and prolonged droughts, the effects of environmental change have been impossible to ignore this year. With El Nino forecast to intensify, the risks to people, nature and economies are only increasing.

These shocks are unfolding against the backdrop of widespread nature loss, with WWF’s Living Planet Report 2026 finding that the average size of monitored wildlife populations declined by 73 percent between 1970 and 2022. Nature loss is increasingly a question of economic and national resilience – affecting food and water security, health, supply chains and geopolitical stability.

The situation is serious, but science shows there are still grounds for hope.

The economic systems driving nature’s decline can be transformed, and change can accelerate much faster than many may expect. Evidence shows that under the right conditions, positive change can cross a tipping point threshold and become self-reinforcing, making a safer, more resilient future not just possible, but inevitable.

The question is: How can we accelerate the actions needed to trigger those tipping points and accelerate the transition?

Positive tipping points and the opportunity for transformational change

In environmental terms, we often think about tipping points in terms of the threats they pose to vital ecosystems, such as coral reefs or the Amazon rainforest, where constant damage risks compounding and becoming increasingly impossible to reverse. These dangers are real and urgent. However, these tipping point dynamics can also work in our favour.

Three economic systems are driving most of nature’s decline: the energy system that fuels climate change; the global food system that leads to habitat loss and climate change; and the finance system that bankrolls it all. Triggering tipping points in those systems would see them rapidly transform for the better and reduce harm to the climate and nature. Once that threshold is passed, change can happen quickly as knowledge and technology advance, with solutions becoming cheaper and more accessible and as people learn from others. Encouragingly, progress is already under way – not everywhere, and not yet at the scale required – but enough to demonstrate that change is possible.

The world does not lack goals for 2030. What it lacks is the pace of implementation. With the Global Biodiversity Framework, the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Agreement in place, governments have already agreed on a pathway. Focusing on implementing these agreements in full will create the conditions for rapid systemic change.

The global energy system has already passed a tipping point, with the transition away from fossil fuels to renewable energy now accelerating. While far from complete, this transition demonstrates how rapid systemic change is possible, offering valuable lessons for the equally urgent transformation of our food and financial systems.

Twenty years ago, solar power was used mostly in satellites and pocket calculators. Now, it is the cheapest option for new electricity generation in most countries. Affordable solar panels are electrifying rural households and improving the resilience of food and medical supply chains. Renewable technologies are displacing fossil fuels at a pace few people predicted even a decade ago.

Changing the food and finance systems is proving slower but is no less urgent.

To progress towards a food systems tipping point, we need to hit major milestones in the uptake of nature-positive food production and see wider shifts in consumer demand for healthier, more sustainable foods to reinforce and reward this shift. Some progress is under way with efforts to tackle commodity-driven deforestation, and more than 130 countries have national strategic plans for food system transformation, but commitments have not yet translated into the policies and incentives needed to accelerate the transition.

Tipping the finance system so that more finance flows to activities that protect and restore nature than activities that harm it is a fundamental challenge. Reaching this tipping point will require a combination of regulatory change, subsidy reform, and a shift in how the sector values climate and nature as material financial risks. If even a portion of the money currently directed towards harmful activities is redirected to environmental recovery, it could shift the economics of the entire transformation.

Governments meeting at the COP17 biodiversity and COP31 climate conferences have before them a vital opportunity to work together to accelerate the actions needed to trigger positive tipping points and to build resilience into societies and the global economy.

Hidden within the broader picture of global biodiversity decline are inspiring stories of species recovery. Populations of green sea turtles and tigers are rebounding due to dedicated conservation work bringing together governments, communities and organisations.

Creating systemic change will similarly take action from all of us, from governments to businesses, financial institutions, local communities, and individuals. We know where we need to get to and the hurdles we need to overcome together; the task now is to create the conditions in which positive change gathers momentum and starts reinforcing itself.

Building strength and resilience into our natural support system will require the courage to shift from extractive, wasteful economies focused on short-term gain to systems that are sustainable and regenerative for the long-term benefit of all. We have the goals, the solutions and pathways to get there. Yes, there might be setbacks along the way, but science shows nature and the climate can still recover and that change can happen faster than we might think.

articles.title: Visually impaired man's forever experience flying a plane
articles.summary: The Cornwall Flying Scholarship is offering disabled people the chance to fly a small aircraft.
articles.body:
"It's been a forever experience for someone who is disabled," said Michael, 66, who has a visual impairment.

Flynqy Pilot Training in partnership with charity Aerobility is giving disabled people the chance to experience flying for themselves by piloting a light aircraft through its Cornwall Flying Scholarship programme.

Thanks to the initiative Michael, who lives in Cornwall, was given full control by an instructor for a short flight during an event at Cornwall Airport Newquay on 11 September.

"I've been up there ever since," Michael said.

Flynqy said there was a vetting process and anyone from Cornwall or Devon "willing to travel" to Newquay was welcome to apply.

Michael said he was registered visually impaired in 23 April 2023 and had permanent inoperable double vision and in 24 October 2024, he was diagnosed with cognitive impairment meaning he had a delayed sensory response.

"I struggle to cross a road but I can turn around and tell people I've flown an aeroplane," said Michael.

"It's good for your mental health, it's good for your wellbeing... that means everything."

Flynqy Pilot Training said the initiative launched in September provided a pathways for applicants wanting to develop their aviation knowledge and further their pilot training.

Director Zara Dinnacombe said there was two levels, the beginner scholarship where successful applicants could experience a 50-minute trial flight or an intermediate scholarship.

The intermediate scholarship provides applicants with three hours of fully funded flight training, introducing them to the fundamentals of flying and giving them the opportunity to experience formal pilot training first-hand.

Michael paid for a 30-minute flight, which was subsided by Aerobility, where his instructor explained the different systems and what he needed to do.

"I had the controls flying over Padstow up the coast and onto Port Issac," he said.

"It's something to always talk about and look back on no matter what the future holds... it's a forever experience."

Nathan Doidge, 44, was born with cerebral palsy and told he would never do "anything" - but at the age of 33 he gained his pilot's licence.

Through Aerobility, a UK charity dedicated to giving disabled people access to aviation, Doidge begun his training through a scholarship in London in 2009.

His childhood dream became a reality in 2012 when he received his private pilot's licence.

"Ever since I was a kid I wanted to fly but I didn't expect anyone to believe I could even though I did."

Doidge, who lives in Hayle and flies for fun, said this scholarship was a good opportunity for the disabled community to experience the freedom of flight for themselves.

"Doctors said when I was born I wouldn't be able to do anything, so anything's possible," Doidge said.

"When I learned how to fly, it was said I was probably the most disabled pilot in the UK.

"As proud of that as I am, now it's time to pass that baton to somebody else."

He said being able to fly an aircraft was a confidence boost because it was something most "able-bodied people don't do".

Dinnacombe said the scholarship was something the company had always wanted to offer but financially they were not able to until they received a "generous donation" from a local pilot.

"We're hoping to encourage people with a range of disabilities who may not have thought about aviation before into the industry, either for pleasure or possibly as a career if that's something they want to pursue," she said.

Since launching the initiative in September, they have received about 30 applications.

"Whilst the scholarship primarily focuses on physical disabilities, we're also open to applications from people with hidden disabilities, ex-military personal and either adults or children who are living with mental illness in the county and beyond," said Dinnacombe.

Applications close on Sunday, but she is hopeful the scholarship will run again next year.

Pilot and head of training at Flynqy Marshall Cligman said the South West region lacked a number of things that happen in other parts of the country including aviation.

He hopes this scholarship will create a "movement" and more aviation opportunities for the disabled community.

Cligman, who has been a pilot for about 40 years, added: "I love flying, I love my job, but seeing someone get something from it is what moves me more than anything.

Michael said: "We're pigeon-holed and people make judgements about disabled people, but we need to be stimulated.

"We need to get out there and I think it's wonderful that we're accepted to do this."

Andrew Boomer, operations director at Cornwall Airport Newquay, said it was a pleasure to welcome the "superb" scholarship and working with people in the industry was "opening as many doors as we can for as many people as possible".

"In the South West, we're probably leading from the front in terms of offering this opportunity for people who wouldn't otherwise get the opportunity," he added.

Chairman of the Aerobility board of trustees Neil Tucker said: "It's wonderful to be opening up the freedom of flight to people in Cornwall, giving them the chance to learn to fly over one of the most beautiful parts of the UK.

"Opportunities like ours empower people because as we have seen flying massively boosts self-confidence and people's ability to believe they can do anything."

articles.title: Salem, the three-legged cat, is celebrated in Daventry stories
articles.summary: Salem, a much-loved town cat that died this year, will be remembered in stories by local authors.
articles.body:
Three books are set to be published in memory of a beloved three-legged cat who spent his days mingling with shoppers in a high street.

Salem, a favourite in his hometown of Daventry, Northamptonshire, died earlier this year at the age of 15. Locals raised thousands of pounds towards a memorial statue in his honour.

Now a local publisher is set to release three books, containing stories about Salem the cat, with some of the proceeds going into the pot for the bronze statue.

A spokesperson for Discover Daventry said: "Salem brought so much joy to Daventry, and it's wonderful to see him continue to inspire people. Between the statue and these books, his story will be shared for generations."

Members of the town's Suddenly Writing Club worked on creating stories about Salem, with four being chosen for publication.

Cheryl Thallon, the owner of Suddenly on Sheaf Street bookshop said: "We are always looking to publish stories from Daventry authors.

"Our writing club at Suddenly on Sheaf Street bookshop has some really talented writers. We're thrilled to be publishing their stories of Salem."

Those four stories will be released as a collection of three books at the launch event, where Salem's owner Erin Hills will be the special guest.

Proceeds from the book sales will be shared between the publisher, the authors, and Salem's owner, with remaining money put towards the bronze statue.

The Salem Collection of books will be launched at a party at Suddenly on Sheaf Street, a local independent bookshop, on Thursday 15 October.

articles.title: Photographer has 'mythic-like' encounter with rare albino deer
articles.summary: The British Deer Society confirms the photograph is of an albino red deer seen in Devon.
articles.body:
A photographer who captured on camera a rare encounter with a white hart deer in the wilds of Devon said he felt "awe" after coming within feet of the animal.

Brian Johnston, a lorry driver who photographs wildlife in his spare time, said it was following a two-day mission that he finally spotted the stag dozing in a field.

"It really is a spectacle to see this mythic-like creature - and to see one just sitting in a field is pretty special," he said.

Charles Smith-Jones, technical advisor at the British Deer Society, said, after studying the photographs, that he believed the red deer to be "albinistic" - which he said was "very very unusual".

White hart is a term used to describe an adult male red deer with a white coat, although most white deer are actually leucistic - combining a lack of hair and skin pigment with normal eye and nose colour.

True albinos were more rare, said Smith-Jones of the British Deer Society .

"You run into them every now and then - you get localised populations where the gene is reasonably strong.

"Some of them are albinos, some are leucistic, which means they have less [melanin] which causes colouration."

Steve Hussey, from the Devon Wildlife Trust, meanwhile, warned against revealing the deer's whereabouts to protect its welfare.

Johnston, 42, said he had taken up wildlife photography about four years ago and had since captured many pictures of deer.

However, it was only during the short period of rutting season that he had spotted the rare white hart deer, he added - believing them to be leucistic.

He said: "I'm out most weekends, especially when the stags come out of hiding.

"I saw this one last year but it's bigger now, with more spikes on its antlers."

Describing the stags as "elusive" and "really impressive", he said getting close to them was a "challenge" while having captured the image was a "good feeling".

"Not many people get to see them," he added.

"The day before we spotted it but it got a whiff of our scent and ran off.

"The next day he was dozing in a field so we managing to get fairly close."

articles.title: Blue drum case: Future of Muskan's 10-month-old daughter  hangs in the balance
articles.summary: MEERUT: The future of 10-month-old Radha remains uncertain after her mother, Muskan Rastogi, was sentenced to death on Wednesday for murdering her
articles.body: MEERUT: The future of 10-month-old Radha remains uncertain after her mother, Muskan Rastogi, was sentenced to death on Wednesday for murdering her husband, merchant navy officer Saurabh Rajput, in the Meerut ‘blue drum’ case.However, jail authorities said the infant would continue living with her mother for now, as the sentence would not be carried out immediately.Radha has been staying with Muskan at Meerut district jail since her birth. Under prison rules, children can remain with their incarcerated mothers until they turn six.Muskan’s elder daughter, seven-year-old Pihu, is believed to be living separately with her maternal grandparents.Senior Jail Superintendent Dr Viresh Raj Sharma said the death sentence would not immediately affect Radha’s living arrangements, as the legal process would take time.“The convicts have the option of appealing before the high court and the Supreme Court, followed by filing mercy petitions before the governor and the president,” Sharma said.He added that a decision on Radha’s future would be taken once an execution date was fixed.Radha was born on November 24 last year at a medical college in Meerut and was taken back to the district jail with Muskan after delivery. At the time, jail officials said both mother and child were healthy and that the infant would receive medical care, nutrition and other necessities.According to Sharma, Muskan has expressed concern about what would happen to her younger daughter. She had also been seeking permission to meet Pihu for the past three to four days, but the meeting had not taken place by the time the sentence was pronounced.The jail administration is yet to decide whether Muskan and her partner, Sahil Shukla, will remain in Meerut jail or be shifted to another prison. Sharma said the decision would be taken after officials receive the detailed court order.Questions remain over Radha’s paternityRadha’s future has also been linked to questions about her paternity. Saurabh’s family had sought a DNA test, with his elder brother saying they would accept the child if it was established that she was Saurabh’s daughter. However, there is no known record of a DNA test being conducted so far.With Muskan and Sahil sentenced to death, responsibility for Radha’s long-term care remains unresolved. For now, she will continue to stay with her mother in jail while the case moves through the appeals process.Muskan and Sahil were convicted on September 30 of killing Saurabh on March 3, 2025, dismembering his body and concealing the remains in a blue drum filled with cement. A section of the M60 was closed after a police incident lead to part of the route being shut in both directions, causing long rush-hour delays.

Drivers were warned to expect delays of more than 30 minutes after a stretch of the motorway was closed between Junction 17 at Prestwich and Junction 18 at Simister Island.

Greater Manchester Police were at the scene alongside North West Ambulance Service and fire crews, National Highways said.

In a statement released after 07:45 BST, the force said it had been responding to concerns for a woman's welfare but she was safe and the road was reopened shortly afterwards.

Three miles (4.8km) of congestion had been reported on the approach to the closure.

articles.title: El Salvador's Bukele announces plan to free up to half of prisoners jailed in gang crackdown
articles.summary: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele unveiled a plan to free up to half of 90,000 detainees arrested under the state of emergency targeting gangs.
articles.body: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has unveiled a plan that could allow the conditional early release of up to half of those detained under a state of emergency that authorities used to arrest more than 90,000 people in the past four and a half years as part of an effort to curb violent criminal gang activity. Bukele's plan to cut the prison population was announced on Tuesday night. It would focus on freeing prisoners who were deemed gang collaborators, a broad term that can include various people, including gang lookouts and those who make extortion payments. "There are many people who have indeed committed crimes, but their crime was collaborating with gangs," Bukele said. "They deserve to be in jail, but we come from a country where collaborating with gangs wasn’t so unusual, and if we were to arrest everyone who collaborated with gangs, we would have to arrest 20% of the population." Without offering details, the president indicated that authorities plan to analyze cases to determine potential early release with monitoring, which could apply to half of the people detained during the state of emergency. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SAYS FEDERAL AUTHORITIES HAVE ARRESTED MORE THAN 10,000 SUSPECTED GANG MEMBERS The state of emergency was declared in March 2022 after a surge in violence left more than 60 people dead in a single day. The measure was initially imposed for 30 days but has been repeatedly extended. The emergency declaration has coincided with a dramatic decline in the country's homicide rate and helped make El Salvador a more appealing tourist destination while also suspending or restricting certain constitutional protections, including the right to be informed of the reasons for detention, the right to access legal counsel and the right to visitation. El Salvador's president has maintained that the measure was needed to rein in rival gangs MS-13 and Barrio 18. Human rights groups, meanwhile, have denounced the declared emergency, arguing that it has sparked widespread arbitrary arrests. The groups have repeatedly demanded that Bukele scrap the measure. NICOLAS MADURO AND WIFE CILIA FLORES FACE NEW CHARGE OF CONSPIRACY TO TORTURE AMERICANS Human rights organizations have recorded more than 6,000 complaints during the emergency declaration and documented the deaths of at least 575 people in government custody. The potential release of thousands of prisoners, some argue, is not enough to repair the damage of their prolonged imprisonment. "The victims of arbitrary detentions don’t just deserve to recover their freedom, but they also deserve to be compensated for the harms caused by the State of El Salvador: the physical and mental harm that imprisonment causes, family suffering, loss of work or studies, reputational damage, among others," exiled Salvadoran lawyer Bertha Deleón wrote on X. Bukele dismissed widespread criticism from national and international human rights groups, suggesting that they should take the side of the victims of gang violence. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The president also defended the need to keep the state of emergency while also indicating his goal of ending it eventually. El Salvador's homicide rate has fallen dramatically over the past decade, including during Bukele's presidency, according to government figures. The rate dropped from a peak of more than 100 murders per 100,000 residents in 2015, four years before Bukele took office, to 1.3 per 100,000 in 2025. But the government has narrowed the definition of homicide to exclude killings by police, murders in prisons and bodies found in unmarked graves. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Ukraine resumes strikes on Russian refineries as Zelenskiy says 'we're done'
articles.summary: KYIV, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian refineries with a strike at an installation in the Ryazan region, the regional governor s...
articles.body:
KYIV, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian refineries with a strike at an installation in the Ryazan region, the regional governor said on Thursday, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy voiced ‌his anger at a "dangerous" withdrawal of US intelligence.

Since US President Donald Trump's surprise announcement of an energy ceasefire ‌between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday, Kyiv had refrained from attacking Russian refineries, which the US leader had blamed for raising diesel prices on global ​markets.

But Zelenskiy had voiced increasing frustration with Russia's continued attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, which he said on Wednesday had left 600,000 people without power. He warned that Ukraine would not suspend its own attacks indefinitely if Russia did not reciprocate and also criticised what he said was Trump's favouritism toward Russia.

In an interview with the Financial Times published on Thursday, he said Ukraine's patience ‌had run out.

"The block (on attacking refineries) is ⁠out. We're done," he told the newspaper.

Pavel Malkov, the governor of Ryazan, said in a post on Telegram that a major Ukrainian drone attack on the region had sparked a fire at ⁠an oil refinery.

"The material damage is now being assessed. Emergency services are working at the scene," he said.

In his interview, Zelenskiy criticised Washington's eagerness to strike business deals with Moscow and Trump's apparent admiration for Russia's Vladimir Putin.

Trump on Saturday called for Ukraine to ​replace Zelenskiy ​and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, one day ​after announcing a diesel supply deal with Russia, ‌aiming to lower fuel prices that have soared since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February.

Despite Ukraine's suspension of refinery attacks, Ukrainian officials complained that they had not received any US early-warning alerts in recent days for incoming Russian ballistic missiles.

They also said the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite communications service had been slowed across the country, hampering frontline operations and medium-range strikes against Russian military sites.

Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X that Starshield - the military ‌version of Starlink - was owned and controlled by the US government, which ​decided on any limits on speed.

Zelenskiy has said that Ukrainian military officials ​were warned by their US counterparts that Washington would ​block intelligence unless they halted strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.

In the FT interview Zelenskiy said the ‌suspension was presented to Kyiv as a technical ​glitch, but he dismissed the idea ​that failures of the Starlink satellite system might have been caused by a fault.

"It was not a technical problem, it was the will," he told the FT.

Asked whether Ukraine would be open to halting energy strikes as ​a way of repairing relations with the ‌White House, he told the newspaper he could only agree if in return he was given more US-made ​Patriot interceptors, calling it the "minimum" that would be acceptable.

(Reporting by Daniel Flynn and Rhea Rose Abraham in ​Bengaluru; editing by Tom Hogue, Edwina Gibbs and Jason Neely)

articles.title: An Arizona homebuilder spent years and hundreds of thousands of dollars turning his backyard into one of America’s largest private garden railways, with nearly 4,000 feet of track and hundreds of train cars
articles.summary: An Arizona businessman who made his name in homebuilding and design spent years and hundreds of thousands of dollars turning his backyard into one of the
articles.body: An Arizona businessman who made his name in homebuilding and design spent years and hundreds of thousands of dollars turning his backyard into one of the largest private garden railways in the United States. Dennis Sirrine, began building the Palo Verde & Southwestern Railroad in January 2004. The project eventually featured nearly 4,000 feet of railway track and a collection of hundreds of model train cars.According to the PBS programme Tracks Ahead, Sirrine used his experience in construction to develop the large outdoor railway. The layout included winding tracks, artificial mountains, lakes and rivers, with sections raised several feet above the ground to make the trains easier to see.Sirrine had been interested in model railways from a long time. During his years as a general contractor, he sometimes incorporated railway layouts into the houses he designed. These involved installing wooden shelves near ceiling height, laying tracks on them and allowing model trains to travel through several rooms.His backyard railway, however, was a much larger undertaking. What began as an empty piece of land required extensive construction, repeated modifications and a complicated operating system. Sirrine told PBS that some parts of the railway had to be built more than once before he was satisfied with the results.How an empty backyard became a railwayWhen construction began in January 2004, Sirrine's backyard was largely flat, with no existing railway infrastructure. After studying garden railways elsewhere in the country, he decided that an elevated layout would provide a better viewing experience than tracks placed directly on the ground.The railway was therefore constructed at heights ranging from 30 inches to six feet. According to Sirrine, approximately 1,000 cubic yards of soil were brought onto the property to raise different sections of the layout.The raised tracks allowed visitors to watch the trains without having to bend down or kneel. Sirrine also designed the surrounding landscape to resemble real railway routes, incorporating changes in elevation, curves, lakes and rivers.His previous construction experience helped him undertake the project, but it did not prevent problems. Sirrine said he had worked in the construction industry for 17 years and understood the building process. Even so, several sections did not turn out as planned.He estimated that nearly half the layout had to be removed and rebuilt because of construction problems or incorrect advice about particular methods. Repeating completed work became one of the project's biggest challenges.Electrical problems led to a different operating systemBuilding the tracks was only part of the work. Sirrine also had to develop a system that could operate different types of model locomotives across the extensive railway.The original electrical arrangements involved approximately 1,000 feet of wire and 10,000 feet of conduit. Looking back, Sirrine said he would have preferred battery-powered trains from the beginning.The railway eventually used a combination of battery power and electricity supplied through the tracks. This arrangement also allowed visitors who owned electrically powered locomotives to operate their trains on his layout.Another major challenge involved the turnouts, or switches, which allow trains to move between different tracks. Sirrine had observed electrical switches developing corrosion and operational problems on other garden railways.Concerned about their reliability in Arizona's climate, he chose air-powered switches manufactured by the California and Oregon Coast Railway company in Oregon. The system operated using a compressor rather than relying on electrical switches.Sirrine told PBS that the air-powered system had worked reliably after installation, resolving one of the most difficult operating problems he had faced.The features Sirrine's most proud ofDespite the project's size, Sirrine identified two particular achievements when discussing his railway with PBS- the accuracy of the tracks and the construction of the artificial mountains.The tracks were laser-levelled to keep them straight and ensure smooth changes in elevation. According to Sirrine, visitors had placed video cameras on flatbed railway cars and recorded their journeys around the layout. They were impressed by how smoothly the trains travelled.Meanwhile, the mountains required a different construction method. Sirrine used flat concrete panels designed to resemble rock, breaking them into sections before arranging, grouting and staining them to create realistic desert formations.The resulting landscape formed part of a railway designed to combine model trains with the appearance of natural terrain.You use AI every day. articles.title: 7 years apart, anti-drug activist Parvinder Jhota’s killing revives memories of Neha Shoree murder
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: Seven years after Punjab drug licensing officer Neha Shoree was shot dead in her office, the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Seven years after Punjab drug licensing officer Neha Shoree was shot dead in her office, the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa has brought renewed attention to the risks faced by those who challenge alleged illegal drug sales in the state.The two cases, separated by more than seven years, involved different circumstances and accused persons. But both brought allegations of illegal drug sales into focus and raised questions about the enforcement of laws governing medicines and addictive substances.Shoree, a zonal licensing drug authority, was shot dead in her office in Kharar near Mohali on March 29, 2019. Jhota, 45, was shot dead in Mansa on October 13, 2026, while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs.Four other people were injured in the firing, which was captured during Jhota’s Facebook Live broadcast.Neha Shoree: A licence cancelled and then a killingShoree was selected as a drug inspector through the Punjab Public Service Commission in 2007 and joined the health department in Ropar that October. In 2013, she was given the responsibility of district zonal licensing authority.On March 29, 2019, she was shot dead at her office by Balwinder Singh, a chemist from Morinda whose shop licence she had cancelled in 2009, police said. During her tenure as a drug inspector in Ropar, Shoree had raided shops and seized banned drugs.Her parents alleged that the drug mafia was behind the killing because she had exposed the sale of intoxicants in the Ropar and Kharar region.“We want to question Prime Minister Narendra Modi that you have been assuring to make a drug-free country but here women officers are being killed by drug mafia,” her mother and paternal aunt said, according to a TOI report published on March 31, 2019.The family’s allegations prompted demands for a wider investigation. The then Punjab chief minister, Capt Amarinder Singh, subsequently handed the probe to ADGP Prabodh Kumar, director of the Bureau of Investigation.However, in December 2019, police informed the Punjab and Haryana high court that their investigation had found no involvement of the drug mafia or any other person besides the accused.Shoree’s family continued to question the findings and seek further investigation.In September 2019, the Punjab government approved financial benefits of around Rs 31 lakh for her family. Shoree’s killing had also prompted scrutiny of the licensing process and the circumstances surrounding the accused’s arms licence.Parvinder Singh Jhota: The 2023 dispute that preceded his killingJhota became known in Mansa for confronting medical store owners whom he accused of selling intoxicating pills, synthetic drugs and other prohibited substances. He recorded confrontations and shared videos on social media.His dispute with medical store owner Ashwani Kumar dated back to July 2023. Jhota had allegedly put a garland of shoes around Kumar’s neck in a public confrontation, accusing him of selling synthetic drugs.A case was registered against Jhota, who was arrested and spent nearly two months in jail. He was released on September 11, 2023, after the complainant approached the court to withdraw the complaint.The case against Kumar concerning the alleged sale of prohibited substances remained pending.Jhota continued his campaign. On the morning of October 13, 2026, he reportedly met an elderly man who had bought synthetic drugs from a medical store and took him to Kumar’s shop to question the owner about the alleged sale.The confrontation escalated as Jhota livestreamed it on Facebook. Kumar allegedly pulled out a firearm and opened fire inside the shop before following the injured activist into the street and firing again. Jhota was hit by three bullets and died at Mansa Civil Hospital. Four others were also injured.In the video, Jhota is heard saying, “maar mainu, maar mainu” (kill me).Kumar fled after the shooting and was arrested in Rajasthan’s Salasar on October 14. Police also detained an alleged associate accused of helping him escape.Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, a retired Army serviceman, refused to cremate his son until those responsible were brought to justice.“I am still alive and pledge to fight against the drug peddlers as my son was waging a war against them. I am also ready to take a bullet if the peddlers are not taken to task,” Bhim Singh said at Mansa Civil Hospital.A continuing challenge for PunjabThe killings have brought renewed attention to the state’s efforts to curb drug abuse and the alleged illegal sale of addictive pharmaceutical substances. Following Jhota’s murder, the Punjab government stepped up inspections of chemist shops.The two cases must be viewed in their individual contexts: Shoree was a government officer carrying out licensing duties, while Jhota was an activist who publicly confronted people he accused of selling prohibited substances.Investigators in Shoree’s case said they found no evidence of anyone else being involved in her murder, while the investigation into Jhota’s killing concerns a separate accused and a separate dispute.Their deaths, years apart, have nevertheless renewed questions about the availability of addictive substances, the enforcement of drug-sale regulations and the safety of people who seek to expose alleged violations.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news.
