articles.title: A UK man collected more than £10,000 through fake GoFundMe and JustGiving appeals by pretending to be a grieving single father; sentenced for 12 weeks after pleading guilty in court
articles.summary: A man from Letchworth Garden City, Hertfordshire, used a heartbreaking story to persuade people to donate more than £10,000 to fake online fundraising
articles.body: A man from Letchworth Garden City, Hertfordshire, used a heartbreaking story to persuade people to donate more than £10,000 to fake online fundraising appeals. Robert Ashton claimed that his partner had died from Covid-19 and that he was left to raise their children alone. People who believed his story donated money through GoFundMe and JustGiving, hoping to help a father going through a difficult time. But the tragedy he described was fabricated, and dozens of people ended up giving money under false pretences.How did the UK man use fake GoFundMe and JustGiving appealsAccording to Hertfordshire Constabulary, Ashton began creating fake social media accounts in early 2020, during the Covid-19 pandemic. He presented himself as a father who had lost his partner, the mother of his children, to the virus and was struggling to cope with the financial pressure of raising his family alone.He directed people to fundraising pages on GoFundMe and JustGiving, asking for money to help cover bills and support his children. The claims appealed to people who wanted to help a family they believed was dealing with bereavement and financial hardship.However, the story was fabricated. Instead of raising money for the reasons described in the appeals, Ashton obtained donations by misleading people about his personal circumstances. His activity continued over several years, eventually bringing in more than £10,000.The human cost of the fundraising fraudThe impact went beyond the amount collected. Hertfordshire Constabulary reported that dozens of people had been affected, with many donors being elderly or vulnerable. Some could barely afford to give away the money they contributed.The donors believed they were helping a bereaved parent and his children during an exceptionally difficult period. Discovering that the story was false meant that their generosity had been exploited.The case also demonstrated how emotional appeals can influence people's decisions. Stories involving the death of a loved one, struggling families and children in need can encourage people to donate quickly, particularly when they believe their contribution will make an immediate difference.Police also warned that there might be further victims who had not reported their experiences or had not realised they had been deceived.Ashton received a prison sentence for his actionsAshton, who was 37 at the time of sentencing and lived in Pascal Way, Letchworth Garden City, pleaded guilty to fraud. On 5 December 2023, St Albans Crown Court sentenced him to 12 weeks in prison and ordered him to pay £290 in compensation to victims, according to Hertfordshire Constabulary.The sentence followed a scheme that had taken advantage of people's willingness to help someone they believed was facing personal tragedy. Although individual donations may have seemed small, together they amounted to more than £10,000.Police urged anyone who believed they had been affected by similar fraud to report it to Action Fraud, the UK's national reporting service for fraud and cybercrime. Reporting suspected scams can help authorities identify patterns of offending and establish whether other people have suffered losses.How crowdfunding platforms work to prevent fraudulent appealsCrowdfunding platforms give people a way to support individuals, families and causes by collecting donations online. However, the ease of setting up and sharing a fundraising page can also create opportunities for people to misrepresent their circumstances.GoFundMe explains that misleading information about an organiser, the intended recipient or the purpose of a fundraiser can raise concerns. The platform encourages people to report suspicious campaigns so they can be reviewed.It also describes safeguards intended to help protect donations. These include identity checks and reviews of fundraising activity by its Trust and Safety team, particularly when organisers prepare to withdraw money.Such measures can help identify problems, but donors should still examine an appeal carefully. A convincing personal story alone does not establish that the organiser's claims are genuine or that donations will be used as promised.What donors should do when a fundraising page looks suspiciousJustGiving provides advice for people who have concerns about a crowdfunding page. Its official guidance recommends contacting the page owner for clarification where appropriate. If the information appears misleading or the money may not be used for the stated purpose, the platform can be contacted to review the concern.Before contributing, donors should check who organised the appeal, who will receive the money and how the funds are expected to be spent.You use AI every day. articles.title: School roof collapse in Pakistan kills at least 27 students and one teacher
articles.summary: At least 27 students, most younger than 13, were killed in Pakistan on Thursday, along with a teacher, when a school roof collapsed during classes in the northwestern city of Peshawar, authorities said, warning that the death toll could rise.
articles.body: ISLAMABAD — At least 27 students, most younger than 13, were killed in Pakistan on Thursday, along with a teacher, when a school roof collapsed during classes in the northwestern city of Peshawar, authorities said, warning that the death toll could rise. Television images showed ambulances rushing to the site at the privately run Al-Khair Education Center while rescuers pulled bloodied students from the rubble. “We have taken out at least 45 children,” said district emergency officer Iftikhar Khan, adding that more were reported to be buried in the rubble. Rescue teams were working to extricate bodies and take the injured to hospital, said government official Bilal Faizi. Twenty injured and most of the dead were brought to the city’s Lady Reading Hospital, its spokesperson, Mohammad Asim, said. A rescue official said the ceiling came down on the students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two stories. Authorities said an investigation had been ordered to determine the cause. Peshawar police chief Mian Saeed said he feared the death toll could rise as just 47 of the 110 students in three classrooms at the time had been rescued. “It was a weak building structure,” Saeed added. “Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse.” There was no immediate comment from school officials.

articles.title: School roof collapses in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 29 people
articles.summary: At least 28 students and one teacher killed in incident at Al-Khair Education Centre, a private school in Peshawar.
articles.body:
The roof of a school in northwestern Pakistan has collapsed, killing at least 28 students and a teacher and injuring more than 50 others, authorities said.

The incident happened on Thursday at Al-Khair Education Centre, a private school in Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province .

Lady Reading Hospital spokesman Mohammad Asim confirmed the casualties, saying some of the injured were in critical condition. All the children killed or injured were age 13 or younger, he said. The hospital has declared an emergency as medical staff treat the wounded.

Hours after the collapse, rescue officials said everyone trapped under the rubble had been recovered.

Reporting from Islamabad, Al Jazeera’s Kamal Hyder said the school had about 350 registered students.

“The casualties are likely to rise. Dozens of wounded students are in hospital. Some of them are in a serious condition,” he added.

Authorities said an investigation has been ordered to determine the ⁠cause of the collapse.

“Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country. My heartfelt condolences and prayers are with the bereaved families,” Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar said in a post on X.

“The prime minister and the government have taken serious note of the situation. Ensuring the safety and protection of our children must remain paramount,” he added.

articles.title: ‘Our works are next to each other’: Art bridges Gaza and West Bank
articles.summary: Young Palestinian artists in Gaza and the occupied West Bank bring their work together in simultaneous exhibitions.
articles.body:
Bethlehem, occupied West Bank – Artists arrived with family and friends at the Bethlehem Peace Center, where a live feed connected them to a small gathering at an artist’s studio in Bureij refugee camp, in the central Gaza Strip.

The two exhibitions marked the opening of Anamel Falasteen, the first competition organised by Falasteen Collective, a cultural initiative launched in 2025 by Palestinian artists, filmmakers, designers and others working in arts and culture. The three-day twin exhibitions, held earlier this week, brought together young Palestinian artists whose work and opportunities to meet are separated by Israeli movement restrictions.

“In the competition, we have Palestinian artists from Jerusalem, historic Palestine, the Gaza Strip and the West Bank,” said Osama Nazzal, one of the judges, speaking in Bethlehem. “I don’t like these divisions. I want to say all of Palestine.”

From his studio at Gallery Paleta in Gaza’s Bureij refugee camp, amid Israel’s ongoing genocidal war on the Palestinian enclave, painter and juror Ghanem Al Den sent greetings on the live feed.

“Greetings and peace from soul to soul, from Gaza to our sister Palestinian cities across this beloved homeland,” he said.

“In this competition, many things that were lost came together. The most important thing is hope.”

After the speeches, visitors had the opportunity to take a closer look at the paintings, photographs and drawings that covered the walls. Visitors moved between them, stopping to look closer, point and talk about what they saw.

“Artists decided to come from Hebron, from Ramallah, from Jerusalem, from Jaffa, from Nablus, despite the risk,” said Mohamed Abusrour, one of the founding members of Falasteen Collective.

“They have a voice, they want to contribute, and they want to show the world that we still exist.”

Not all the works on display in Bethlehem were originals. Because of the blockade and movement restrictions, the organisers said there was no way to transport original artworks out of Gaza. Instead, they printed reproductions of the Gaza submissions and hung them alongside original pieces.

For one Bethlehem visitor, the curation was what stood out. She assumed some works exploring similar themes were by the same artist. They turned out to be by different artists, some in Gaza and others in the West Bank.

“I sat a bit longer with some paintings, and that brought tears to my eyes,” she said. “The livestream with the presence of everyone’s paintings was a portal to bringing everyone’s essence together.”

Young artists document loss and everyday life

The works on display reflected different ways of documenting Palestinian life, from the loss of family and home in Gaza to the traditions and everyday experiences artists want to preserve.

Abusrour said the idea for the competition came from listening to artist friends describe how they could not participate or express themselves freely. He said the aim was to give young Palestinians a platform to show their work at home and abroad “without any restriction”.

The competition was open to artists aged 15 to 30. About 170 applied, nearly 60 percent from Gaza, according to the organisers. A jury split between the West Bank and Gaza selected 120 works across three tracks: memory and place, land and return, and everyday heritage.

The jury met daily by video, working through power and internet cuts in Gaza.

“Despite the lack of resources, they decided to take part, and when they decided to take part, they decided to take part with strength,” Abusrour said of the artists in Gaza.

Among the works shown in Gaza was The Vine Bears Witness, by Arwa Mukhaimer, a 20-year-old university student. It shows the entrance to her family’s home, shaded by a grapevine. It was there, on March 30, 2024, that she received news of her father’s death. He had been unable to get medical treatment during Israel’s war on Gaza, she said. Five months later, she said, the house was destroyed.

“This painting is a memorial to what we lost, a double loss, of the father and of the place,” she told Al Jazeera.

Two days before he died, he told her: “My darling, may God be pleased with you.” She wrote those words into the painting.

When she was displaced as a result of the war, she said, “The first thing I thought about was my tools.” Art supplies are hard to find in Gaza, she said, and some materials never enter the Strip.

The challenges facing artists extend beyond access to materials. Gaza’s main art spaces, including the Eltiqa and Shababeek galleries, have been destroyed as a result of Israeli attacks in Gaza.

Mukhaimer said her painting “has hope and joy in it, but its meaning is painful and moving”.

In Bethlehem, Hanan Barghouthi, 24, a visual artist from Ramallah, also chose to paint joy, but from a different place. Her painting of a Palestinian wedding is filled with bright colours, traditional symbols, and movement.

“All the art has become about people expressing sadness, so I want to reflect happiness, because I like to be happy,” she said.

Movement restrictions divide Gaza and the West Bank

Bringing the two exhibitions together required organisers to work around the restrictions that keep Palestinians in the two territories apart. Artists in Gaza and the West Bank live under different conditions of Israeli occupation, but both face barriers to meeting, collaborating and exhibiting together.

Israel has imposed a land, sea and air blockade on the Gaza Strip since June 2007 . In the occupied West Bank, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) documented 925 obstacles restricting the movement of 3.4 million Palestinians, including in East Jerusalem, as of December 2025.

That separation is not accidental, said Rehab Nazzal, an artist and educator on the competition’s advisory committee.

“It’s a creation of the settler colonial project,” she said. “By suffocating the Palestinians with all the restrictions of movement, it intends to push the Palestinians out.”

Abusrour said spaces like the exhibition give young Palestinians a reason to stay and continue creating.

“You cannot live in a place, and be called steadfast, without having a reason to live as well,” he said.

Watching the Gaza artists on screen, Barghouthi said she felt “very sad” and asked herself, “Where are we and where are they?”

“I felt we were close to them, but at the same time far away,” she said. “But emotionally, I felt they were next to us, because our works are next to each other.”

articles.body: LUCKNOW: Model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma in Lucknow, has released another video on Thursday claiming that the two had been dating for the past two months and that Sharma was under a massive debt.In the five-minute-long video, Dubey recounted the events leading up to Sharma’s death.Dubey alleged that Sharma had been receiving calls from people he had borrowed money from and had repeatedly told her that he would die by suicide if he could not repay the loans.She said she could show screenshots to support her claims.In the video, Dubey also appealed to people to stop harassing her, warning that she would die by suicide if the alleged torture continued.“Think why would someone kill someone and throw them from their own apartment,” she said, questioning the allegations against her.She urged the media not to spread rumours without evidence. Referring to Sharma’s mother, Dubey alleged that she had started a quarrel with her driver in the hospital. She then said, “It's not like you have lost a son, I have lost my boyfriend.”Dubey claimed that she and Sharma had not spoken to each other for six to seven days before the incident. On October 7, Sharma allegedly contacted her driver through a tea vendor and was crying, she said."Then I called him twice from my number. He did not pick up the call at that time. Later, he called me around 2am. I asked him what happened to which he asked me to meet him. We met, went to cafe where he ordered coffee for me and juice for himself," she said, adding that he had a "lot of beers" before meeting her."Later, both of us went to my place. While he drove my car, my driver took his car," she said.Dubey said her sister, Rashmi, visited her home on October 8 to discuss a puja for Navratri. She denied her sister's involvement in the case, claiming that Rashmi barely knew Sharma and had hardly spoken to him."My sister has nothing to do with this case. She did not even know Shiva that well. She never spoke to him...My sister and I, we went for a walk that evening. Shiva's friends joined us - one of them was Ashwini Mishra and other named Harsh. We all went for a long drive. I spoke to Shiva, his mother, brother-in-law, and sister too that day," she said.Recounting the day Sharma died, Dubey claimed that he appeared depressed on October 9. She said they woke up and made tea before he went to the washroom."I don't even know what it was. We woke up, made tea. Shiva went to the washroom. Usually, he would never close the main gate. But this time, he did. I asked my sister to go check up on him after a while. As soon as she opened the gate, he jumped from the balcony," she said.Dubey alleged that Sharma's mother accused them of murder and assaulted her driver when she arrived at the hospital."It will be recorded on the hospital's camera. Without knowing anything, she accused us of murder. Without thinking, she blamed us for murder. She blamed us so badly that we might not be able to get out of that blame for life," she said.The 1st videoEarlier, Dubey had released another video denying any wrongdoing and claiming that Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder.She also urged the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials, saying she was willing to appear before the police and record her statement.“Just because someone follows me or is connected to me on Instagram does not mean I know them or have any relationship with them,” she had said.Dubey had also denied being absconding and claimed she wanted to cooperate with investigators.“I am not missing. I want to come before the police and tell them everything I know. I want to place the complete truth before them,” she said in the earlier video.Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. According to police sources, he had been in a relationship with Dubey for around four months.Following his death, Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, lodged an FIR accusing Dubey, her sister Rashmi, driver Adil and others of murdering her son. articles.title: Sam Heughan joins battle against Chapelcross data centre
articles.summary: Sam Heughan questions the economic benefits of a massive development proposed at Chapelcross near Annan.
articles.body:
Outlander star Sam Heughan has joined the campaign against plans to build a giant data centre at a former nuclear site in the south of Scotland.

The actor - who grew up in Galloway - questioned how much financial benefit projects like the one at Chapelcross, near Annan, would deliver to Scotland.

He said the actual number of jobs delivered after the construction phase had been completed would be "very few".

CX Tech Ltd, which is behind the plans, said it could deliver more than 500 full-time posts and represented a "once-in-a-generation opportunity" for the region.

In an interview on Storm & Alexis on 5, Heughan said he had only recently found out about the data centre planned in Dumfries and Galloway - one of a large number planned across Scotland.

"There's a lot to find out here and many causes for concern, I think," he said.

"The only people who are building these large-scale, hyper scale data centres are US tech giants.

"The financing will go back to them, the benefits will go back to them."

Giant data centre plans lodged for old nuclear plant site

He added that he also had concerns about the impact on the landscape.

"They're being built on, not just on brown land, but also agricultural land, protected grassland," he said.

"There's an impact to the environment, there's impact to the animals that live near there.

"There needs to be just more legislation and more consideration

"We shouldn't blindly go into this and keep investing in it. I think a pause or moratorium is the right way to start this."

He said that after working on Outlander for 12 years he had seen a "huge rise" in tourism and much greater awareness of Scotland's "amazing landscape" and "incredible buildings".

"There's so much that Scotland has to offer, not only in terms of tourism but also our exports," he added.

"So should we even be investing in these large industrial sites that are essentially going to become wasteland?".

The plans for Chapelcross were lodged last month and have already attracted considerable opposition.

Dumfries and Galloway Council confirmed that due to the "significant volume" of representations it has received it will not publish them online in the usual way in order to reduce pressure on its planning service.

Instead, the number of representations for and against the plans will be published along with a summary of the grounds for commenting.

Graeme Anderson, chief executive of CX Tech, said Chapelcross had the potential to bring together renewable energy, digital infrastructure and high-value jobs.

He said it could create a "new economic future" for a site which had played an important role in Scotland's energy story for generations.

CX Tech hopes work could start on the project next year with it taking about eight years to complete.

It said the project was in line with attempts to redevelop the site and could support up to 750 jobs during construction and about 540 once it was operational.

The Scottish government has rejected a call from the Scottish Greens for the application processes for data centres to be paused until new national guidelines are in force.

However, ministers said they would publish the guidance by Christmas - and that they did not expect any planning decisions to be made before then.

articles.title: Rubio push on Greenland delivers a huge diplomatic win for US against China
articles.summary: Marco Rubio's diplomatic sweep from Panama to Iceland aims to secure critical sea lanes and box out China's threat to United States interests.
articles.body: China seeks to replace the United States as the leading global superpower and key to its strategy is securing critical sea lanes. The country that can control the fate of sea lanes will have leverage over markets and the kind of system on which global trade will rely, access to limited natural resources and a significant ability to project power far from its shores. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has been planning and executing a diplomatic sweep from Panama to Greenland, and now Iceland, to box out China, protect its access and interests and establish an American advantage over the long term. About 40 years ago, President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met in Reykjavík, Iceland, and initiated the start of the thaw of Cold War tensions. Rubio returned to the site of the meeting where Reagan refused to surrender his vision of a space-based missile shield to the Soviets and reminded the world that the High North still matters for American power and interests. Standing side by side with Iceland’s foreign minister, Rubio noted that the location remains a "critical outpost for monitoring clandestine behavior and deterring our adversaries." When a reporter asked him if the United States may expand its military footprint there, he didn’t commit to plans but emphasized that doing so would require Icelandic consent. The negotiations will continue, and, though he didn’t mention Russia or China by name, those are the nations now posing acute threats to the United States and its allies. TRUMP'S GREENLAND OBSESSION ISN’T RANDOM. HERE’S WHAT’S AT STAKE The Reykjavík visit follows the recently secured landmark deal with the Kingdom of Denmark. This deal ensures that the United States can prevent the Chinese from establishing its habitual scheme in the Arctic. Critics of the deal have said that the negotiations between Washington and Copenhagen were "much ado about nothing," considering that China isn’t (yet) in Greenland. This misses the point. As the ice melts, Arctic shipping routes are becoming increasingly navigable, creating new sea lanes (and thus choke points) that will shape global shipping and military posturing for decades to come. The agreement gives Washington the authority to block non-NATO commercial and military presence in Greenland, a direct role in screening and accelerating foreign investment in critical sectors, overflight, missile defense access and unrestricted undersea access across Greenland’s territorial waters. TRUMP DECLARES VICTORY IN HISTORIC DEAL WITH GREENLAND AS HE SECURES 'PERMANENT' US MILITARY RIGHTS Critically, the deal honors Greenland’s sovereignty, a non-negotiable issue for Denmark, while remaining in force in perpetuity, regardless of if Greenland were to ever become independent. In doing so, the deal clarifies where the 1951 treaty was silent. Dismissing the deal, perhaps due to a desire to deny the Trump administration credit, also shortchanges the Danes’ very real concessions and diplomatic skill. Furthermore, the deal came just in time for NATO, whose steadfast solidarity is key as Russia ramps up its campaign of terror attacks across the alliance to collapse support for Ukraine. For years, both the Chinese and Panamanian governments denied China was taking over the Panama Canal. But the president said that the Chinese had illegally stationed soldiers to operate the canal, and a Chinese-owned company was illegally charging for passage to the disadvantage of the United States, which has paid billions to maintain the canal, of which 72% of all vessels (according to the U.S. government) are transiting to or from an American port. That is, making maximalist demands, including threats of aggression against trusted allies in the hopes of getting a deal somewhere short of the opening threat, but close to it. Progress toward the deal only began once Trump stopped making threats in response to the blowback. articles.title: ‘We’re done’: Ukraine resumes strikes on Russian oil refineries as anger mounts with Trump
articles.summary: Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy angrily accused the United States of betraying Kyiv with the “dangerous” withdrawal of support critical to its defense against Russia.
articles.body: Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy angrily accused the United States of betraying Kyiv with the “dangerous” withdrawal of support critical to its defense against Russia. Ukraine held off on attacks for three days after President Donald Trump’s unilateral “energy ceasefire” announcement, but accused Russia of repeatedly attacking its power grid. Zelenskyy voiced mounting frustration over the Kremlin’s failure to abide by the truce, and what he sees as U.S. attempts to pressure Kyiv after gaps in intelligence sharing on Russian attacks and restrictions on the Starlink internet service. Satellite internet functionality while in motion via Starshield — the military version of the SpaceX service — had been restored Thursday morning, according to a source in Ukraine’s defense ministry, speaking on the condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the topic. In an interview with the Financial Times, published early Thursday, Zelenskyy indicated his patience had already been exhausted. “The block (on attacking refineries) is out. We’re done,” Zelenskyy was quoted as saying. Hours later a fire was reported at an oil refinery in the western Ryazan region, Gov. Pavel Malkov said. The Russian defense ministry said Ukraine had “attempted a massive attack on the Ryazan oil refinery.” Ukraine has been reeling from a sudden shift from Trump, who struck a diesel deal with Russia in an apparent bid to relieve pressure at the pump ahead of the Midterm elections. He then demanded that Ukraine stop attacking Russian oil facilities and called for Zelenskyy to be replaced as leader. Trump’s “energy ceasefire” appeared to take both sides by surprise. He has blamed the Ukrainian campaign for fueling a rise in energy prices, despite the impact of his own war with Iran. The moves caused frustration and confusion in Ukraine and Europe, intensifying concerns over how much of an ally the U.S. remained in the fight against Russia. That worry was exacerbated Wednesday when Kyiv said it was facing the slowing down of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite terminals, disrupting battlefield missions and its ability to intercept Russian drones attacking Ukrainian cities. Ukraine was swarmed by Russian drones on Wednesday, and since midnight on Thursday more than 850 had filled Ukraine’s skies, Zelenskyy said. “And this comes precisely at a time when the speed of our defensive capabilities is being artificially restricted,” he said, referring to the Starlink slowdown. Musk, a staunch ally of Trump, wrote on social media that decisions on restricting the use of Starshield, the military version of his company’s satellite system, were up to the U.S. military and ultimately Trump. Overnight, Musk said it was “time for Zelenskyy to go.” The defense ministry source said Kyiv was still seeking clarification on the reasons for Wednesday’s throttling of the technology, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communication, drone operations and air defense. It came amid mounting questions about whether the U.S. has stopped or limited the sharing of critical military intelligence with Ukraine, after Zelenskyy said several ballistic strikes on Kyiv did not come with the usual advance warning from its partners. Coming only days after Trump eased sanctions on Russia’s diesel exports and railed against Zelenskyy, European and Ukrainian officials told NBC News they believed that the moves were likely aimed at pressuring Kyiv into making concessions at the negotiating table amid a stalemate in peace talks. Ukraine was concerned that the chain of events amounted to an effort to pile pressure on Kyiv and backtrack on years of U.S. promises to help fend off the Russian invasion, one of the Ukrainian officials said. Ukraine relies heavily on U.S. intelligence and the Starshield satellite network to defend itself against Russian drone and missile attacks and to target Russian forces with its own drones. A reduction in intelligence assistance or satellite access could seriously undermine Ukraine’s battlefield prospects just as winter sets in, according to military experts. Ukrainian military officials were told by their U.S. counterparts that “if you will not stop [the energy strikes], we will block intelligence,” Zelenskyy said, according to FT, although it was subsequently presented to Kyiv as a technical glitch. The withdrawal of the intelligence and simultaneous weakening of Starlink satellite internet were “dangerous” for Ukraine at a time when Russia is intensifying its strikes, he told the newspaper, adding that fighting without the U.S. would be “very difficult.” In a separate interview with Piers Morgan on Wednesday, Zelenskyy said he felt “betrayed” by Trump’s actions. The White House did not immediately respond to an overnight request for comment on Zelenskyy’s accusations and the renewed Ukrainian strikes.

articles.title: Altnagelvin: No money for new emergency department, minister says
articles.summary: Robbie Butler says a new ED at Altnagelvin hospital in Derry is a priority but he does not have the money to pay for it.
articles.body:
A new emergency department (ED) at Altnagelvin hospital remains a priority project but there is currently no funding for it, Northern Ireland's health minister has said.

Robbie Butler, who visited the Londonderry hospital on Wednesday, said a new ED would be "incredibly high on the project list if the money becomes available".

A new ED is one of two Western Health and Social Care Trust priority capital projects and has an estimated cost of around £73m.

Altnagelvin's emergency department - the oldest one operating around-the-clock in Northern Ireland - was designed to treat about 40,000 patients a year but is now dealing with up to twice that amount.

The minister said the ongoing work by the trust had helped mitigate the waiting times at the ED but that these were still "much too long".

"People living in this area will know that acutely," he said. "They're messaging me, they're emailing me, and I hear those messages.

"But the senior leadership team of the Western Trust, like me, have an ambition to see that reset and transformed.

"If the money became available, I would say the case has been well made."

In July 2025, the trust submitted revised proposals for the new emergency department at Altnagelvin to the Department of Health.

At that time, Butler's predecessor Mike Nesbitt told the Stormont Assembly that any progress would depend on the availability of both capital funding and the running costs.

Meanwhile, Butler also told BBC News NI the Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant had fallen short in relation to what is being offered on the budget.

The executive has not agreed a budget for this year, blaming the UK's devolution funding formula for leaving it short.

Extra funding of about £1.5bn would be released in three tranches, with £525m available this year.

Bryant has accused executive ministers of being financially "irresponsible".

Butler said: "I don't agree with the Secretary of State on this because we are not funded at the agreed level of need."

articles.title: ‘Each country goes its own way’: How Balkan politics shape ties with Israel
articles.summary: Countries’ ties with Israel reflect local politics, defence deals and strategic interests rather than a united stance.
articles.body:
Throughout Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, Europe’s position has, to an extent, been aligned.

Outliers such as Spain and the Republic of Ireland have long been more vocal in condemning Israel, but overall, the shift from unconditional solidarity with Israel to concern over its conduct has taken hold in much of the continent.

Across the Balkans, divergent policies towards Israel reflect domestic calculations, transactional diplomacy, and unresolved identity politics rather than a shared vision for the Middle East, according to experts.

“The Balkan countries have almost no common positions at all, and so it’s not surprising their positions towards Israel and Gaza are all over the map,” Marko Prelec, analyst at the International Crisis Group, told Al Jazeera. “Each country goes its own way.”

Prelec noted that while there is genuine revulsion towards Israeli policy in Gaza and sympathy for Palestinians – particularly among Bosnian Muslims – most countries in the region take their positions based on unrelated interests.

Florian Bieber, professor of Southeast European history and politics at Austria’s University of Graz, said regional consensus is nearly impossible.

“The position towards Israel is strongly shaped by domestic politics and also national narratives, which makes a regional or even a country-specific position unlikely,” Bieber told Al Jazeera.

Bosnia and Herzegovina: Differences from one entity to another

Nowhere is this fragmentation more evident than in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where the war in Gaza has deepened existing ethno-national divisions.

Bosniak political representatives and much of the public in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina have expressed strong solidarity with Palestinians, while leaders in Republika Srpska have been openly pro-Israel, and some Croat political figures have also adopted a more sympathetic tone towards Israel.

“Bosniak solidarity with Palestinians is often seen not just through an ideological lens, but also from the perspective of war and being a victim of Serb nationalist aggression, comparing the Palestinian experience with the Bosniak experience in the 1990s,” Bieber explained.

Conversely, leaders in the Serb-majority entity, Republika Srpska, led by former President Milorad Dodik, have openly embraced Israel.

Foreign policy analyst and journalist Bosko Jaksic told Al Jazeera that for Dodik, “The enemy of my enemy is my friend – Jews and Orthodox Serbs against Muslims. This religious and ethnic factor allows him to maintain an Israeli connection parallel to his closeness with Russia, while simultaneously performing a new American flip by glorifying [US President] Donald Trump .”

Prelec added that Bosnian Serb outreach to Israel and specifically Likud, the ruling Israeli party, represents “an attempt to find allies for its internationally unpopular flirtation with separatism, and an indirect way to strengthen ties with parts of the MAGA [Make America Great Again] movement and the Trump administration”.

Serbia: Arms sales and multi-vector balancing

In Serbia, the approach to Israel blends defence economics with foreign policy.

Despite historically friendly relations with Palestine and voting in favour of Palestinian membership in international bodies, Belgrade has exported ammunition and arms to Israel since October 2023.

The relationship has also moved beyond exports. In September, Serbia opened an Israeli-linked drone assembly plant , underlining the growing practical dimension of bilateral defence cooperation.

Vuk Vuksanovic, lecturer in foreign policy and grand strategy at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera that Serbia’s defence industry “has not been particularly picky when it comes to its customers, and the desire for profit has been one of the factors”.

However, he emphasised broader geopolitical ambitions.

“In the past three years, there has been a tilt towards Israel regarding security cooperation, while diplomatically Serbia tries to be cautious in multilateral institutions due to its ties with the wider Islamic world,” he said.

Vuksanovic noted that Belgrade views Israel as a partner to “acquire the protection of Israeli lobby groups and access to the Trump administration in the US”, especially as the Serbian government faces domestic political opposition.

Meanwhile, Jaksic warned of the international risks involved.

“Due to the significant increase in ammunition exports to Israel during the war in Gaza, Serbia risks being accused of complicity in genocide,” he said. “Beyond financial calculations, the Serbian president attempts to use closeness with his ideological, authoritarian, and nationalist ally, [Israeli Prime Minister] Benjamin Netanyahu, to get closer to Trump.”

Kosovo, Albania, and the Washington anchor

For Kosovo and Albania, foreign policy regarding Israel remains anchored to security alliances with Washington.

Under the 2020 Washington Agreement, Kosovo recognised Israel in exchange for Israeli recognition of Kosovo’s independence, subsequently opening its embassy in Jerusalem. Serbia, which had pledged in 2020 to move its embassy to Jerusalem, ultimately did not do so.

Pristina opened its Jerusalem embassy “defying the stance of the wider international community”, said Jaksic.

“Israel’s growing influence in the Western Balkans is evident,” he noted. “That includes investments, and in the case of Serbia, especially military cooperation. This absolutely does not exclude personal attempts to buy political impunity from American sanctions, or to ease diplomatic pressure.”

In neighbouring Albania, Prime Minister Edi Rama’s government has preserved warm political ties with Israel.

Driven partly by operational defence needs, Albania deepened cooperation with Israeli cybersecurity companies after cyberattacks, while aligning broader diplomacy with Washington and Brussels.

Executive rifts and ideological turnarounds

In Croatia, foreign policy on Gaza has been paralysed by a sharp executive rift between conservative Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic and President Zoran Milanovic of the Social Democratic Party.

Plenkovic’s government has followed a cautious, mainstream European Union approach, while Milanovic has openly condemned Israel’s military conduct in Gaza, labelling it disproportionate and creating a public fracture in the country’s foreign policy leadership.

Further north in Slovenia , there are ideological shifts.

The previous centre-left government adopted firm measures against Israel – such as an arms embargo, a ban on imports from illegal settlements, and a ban on the entry of top officials like Netanyahu – as well as recognising Palestinian statehood.

Conservative forces under Prime Minister Janez Jansa have sought to reverse these policies.

“In Slovenia, we can see the classic left-right division where populist and far-right parties support Israel because of Netanyahu as a similar political actor,” said Bieber. “They recognise him as ideologically aligned, which helps reinforce their view of Islam as a threat, fitting their own narratives.”

Smaller NATO members like Montenegro and North Macedonia have chosen a path of quiet alignment.

Both adhere to standard EU and NATO statements, calling for ceasefires and humanitarian aid while carefully avoiding high-profile bilateral disputes or bold independent diplomatic initiatives.

Further east, Romania and Bulgaria maintain a cautious tone that sometimes leans towards Israel. Grounded in historic bilateral relations and deep strategic defence partnerships with the United States, Bucharest and Sofia balance carefully worded statements at the United Nations with ongoing military and intelligence coordination.

Meanwhile, in Greece, consecutive governments in Athens have maintained a robust strategic military and energy partnership with Israel; Athens recently signed a $3.5bn missile deal with Israel. Originally forged alongside Cyprus to balance regional maritime rivalries in the Eastern Mediterranean, this alliance has held firm despite significant domestic public backlash and protests over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

Ultimately, the disparate responses across the Balkans demonstrate that Middle Eastern policy in the region is rarely about the Middle East itself.

Whether driven by defence profits, constitutional rivalries, or the search for political backing in Washington, regional actors continue to view Israel almost exclusively through a transactional lens.

articles.title: Man killed by tiger died from 'multiple traumatic injuries', inquest hears
articles.summary: William Chapman climbed two fences to enter a tiger's pen at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, an inquest hears.
articles.body:
A man who was attacked by a tiger after climbing two fences to enter its enclosure at a wildlife park died of "multiple traumatic injuries", an inquest has heard.

William Chapman visited Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday and entered the animal's pen.

The 24-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene and died of "multiple traumatic injuries and animal interaction", the opening of his inquest at Doncaster Coroner's Court heard.

Senior coroner Nicola Mundy said he had a history of mental illness, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and had suffered previous bouts of psychosis. His family had raised concerns about his contact with Rotherham, Doncaster and South Humber NHS Trust, the hearing was told.

Chapman was under adult mental health services in Doncaster but was "highly functioning and independent with no care requirements", the inquest heard.

The self-employed online trader was born in Chichester, West Sussex, and living in Doncaster at the time of his death.

Coroner's officer Caitlin Brookes said his family had expressed "a number of concerns" in relation to his contact with mental health services, with the trust launching an investigation following his death.

On Wednesday, a trust spokesperson said it would "never comment on whether someone uses our services or does not use our services".

The BBC approached the trust for further comment.

Brookes told the hearing: "He was approached by the tiger and the ensuing physical contact between the tiger and Mr Chapman led to him sustaining multiple traumatic injuries which rapidly led to his death."

Park staff secured the tiger and paramedics attended but confirmed his death at the scene.

The senior coroner said her office was awaiting a more substantial report as to the extent of his injuries.

Mundy opened the inquest, which his family chose not to attend, on Thursday morning and adjourned proceedings until 18 March 2027.

The incident, which took place shortly after 13:30 BST on Saturday, led to the evacuation of the wildlife park.

An eyewitness described seeing Chapman wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in.

Mobile phone footage, believed to be from Chapman, appears to show the inside of the enclosure as he approaches the tiger across a patch of grass.

The park remains closed and a reopening date is yet to be confirmed.

A park spokesperson previously said the rare Amur tiger involved, called Altai, remained safely in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.

A health and safety investigation has also been launched by City of Doncaster Council.

South Yorkshire Police had provided a number of witness statements from the public and staff who were at the wildlife park at the time, the hearing was told.

Mundy instructed staff to contact Yorkshire Wildlife Park to ask them to keep any relevant CCTV and inform the coroner of any previous visits by Chapman to the park.

articles.body: US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi has warned that anti-Indian hatred and white supremacist ideology can lead to deadly violence after police arrested a 19-year-old man accused of planning a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois.Krishnamoorthi condemned the alleged plan, saying authorities and communities must take threats against Indian Americans seriously before anyone is killed. Police contacted Hindu places of worship within their jurisdiction to warn them about the threat.Suspect held after weapons recoveredPaporakis was arrested as he was leaving his residence. articles.title: Harry and Meghan make first joint appearance since returning to U.K.
articles.summary: LONDON — Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, were making their first royal-style public appearance together on Thursday since they returned to the United Kingdom with their two children.
articles.body: LONDON — Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, were making their first royal-style public appearance together on Thursday since they returned to the United Kingdom with their two children. Harry, 42, and Meghan, 45, were visiting three charities in Nottingham, as they look to rebuild their image in Britain six years after walking away from royal life. Nottingham, a city in central England known as the setting for the famous “Robin Hood” legend, holds a special place in the couple’s history as the place where they made their first joint public appearance after announcing their engagement in 2017. “It’s almost a full circle moment because it looks very much like a royal engagement,” NBC News royal contributor Emily Nash said. The events on Thursday began with a visit to the Community Recording Studio, a youth and community charity in Nottingham that Harry has visited before, including just last year. They were greeted by a cheering crowd, filled largely with young children. Harry and Meghan, who wore a long burgundy coat, stopped to take selfies, give hugs and shake hands. They also spent a few minutes talking to members of the public and the children. The couple were also due to visit the region’s biggest food bank, Himmah, and Epic Partners, which offers disadvantaged young people mentoring programs, sports and education. Noting that the couple will be visiting a charity Harry has a “long history with,” Nash said they were certain to “get a warm reception” given their “long connection with it.” But they have not always received such a warm welcome since their return to the U.K. with Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5. The couple remains locked in a public row with Buckingham Palace about their status and their lack of publicly funded police protection. A letter sent on behalf of King Charles III to senior government and military officials confirmed Harry and Meghan remain nonworking members of the royal family. A spokesperson for the couple told NBC News they were “surprised” by the letter, though they accepted that status when they left Britain for a quieter life in Montecito, an affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara. Their relationship with the royal family has been strained in the years since, with the couple leveling explosive allegations of racism and bullying in their Netflix documentary “Harry & Meghan” and in Harry’s memoir, “Spare.” News of their return to the U.K. sent shockwaves through the British media, and the couple have faced other complications as they settle back into British life. “It was a bit of a bumpy road for Harry and Meghan,” Nash said. “They had to had to move their children from their school after just two days, but I’m told they’re settling in well now and Archie and Lili are very happy at their new school.” The couple’s royal-style visit to Nottingham will renew questions about their security. With or without it, Nash said, “this is them dipping their toe back in the water” and “nothing’s stopping them.” “They don’t need the palace’s permission to do this,” she said.

articles.title: US bank employee stole $280,000 from a vault, then created fake cash-deposit reports to hide it; IRS helped uncover the scheme
articles.summary: Jennifer Lamanna worked at a bank in Florida and stole $280,000 from the bank vault, trying to cover it up by falsifying transaction records.
articles.body: Jennifer Lamanna worked at a bank in Florida and stole $280,000 from the bank vault, trying to cover it up by falsifying transaction records. She deposited some of the stolen cash into an account she controlled and disguised other transactions as legitimate to hide the missing money. She also filed a false cash-deposit report saying a customer deposited more than $160,000 when no such deposit was made. Eventually, the scheme came under federal investigation, and the IRS helped uncover the wrongdoing. Lamanna later pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 15 months in prison.How the bank employee stole $280,000 from the vaultLamanna started stealing money in 2020 while working at an insured financial institution in Venice, Florida, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) said. During the COVID-19 pandemic, reduced staffing arrangements gave her sole access and control over a branch vault, creating an opportunity to remove cash without immediate detection.The DOJ explained that Lamanna initially used a contingency cash bag to take money out of the vault and remove it from the branch. She continued using this method until the bank discontinued the cash bag programme.However, the change did not stop the theft. Lamanna continued taking money from the vault and deposited $255,362 into a bank account under her control. The total amount she stole over several months reached $280,000, according to the IRS.How did she disguise the missing moneyThe missing cash created a problem that Lamanna needed to conceal in the bank's records. According to the DOJ, she made several large withdrawals from a customer's account and followed them with matching deposits. These transactions were intended to make the vault's cash balance appear correct, even though money had been stolen.In fact the customer had not made these deposits. The transactions were designed to give the appearance that the missing cash was accounted for, helping Lamanna to hide the shortfall on the bank's books.The IRS later disclosed Lamanna also submitted fake Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs) to give the transactions a legitimate appearance. These reports are used by banks to report certain large cash transactions to authorities. Lamanna filed false reports to make the activity look legitimate and to avoid suspicion about the missing money.Another layer to the scheme was a fake deposit reportOn June 8, 2023, Lamanna filed a report with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, which is part of the US Treasury Department. The report contained false information, adding another serious offence to the bank theft case.The report claimed that a customer had deposited $160,100 in cash into his bank account. However, the deposit had not taken place. Lamanna knew the statement was false when she submitted it, the IRS said. The false filing showed how the scheme extended beyond the bank's internal records to information submitted to a federal agency.Financial institutions use cash transaction reports to help authorities monitor certain large transactions. Submitting false information can undermine that process by making transactions that never occurred appear genuine. In Lamanna's case, the fabricated report became part of the federal case against her.IRS and FDIC helped investigate the caseThe investigation was conducted jointly by the IRS Criminal Investigation division and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) Office of Inspector General. The two agencies examined the case involving the stolen vault cash, the transactions used to conceal the shortage and the false report submitted to the government. Their work led to federal criminal proceedings against Lamanna. They confirm that the investigation resulted in charges involving both the embezzlement and the false statement.Lamanna was sentenced to 15 months in prisonLamanna pleaded guilty on July 21, 2025, to embezzlement by a bank employee and making a false statement to a government agency. The DOJ announced her guilty plea the following day. As part of the case, Lamanna agreed to forfeit $280,000, representing the proceeds of her criminal conduct.On November 14, 2025, the IRS announced that US District Judge Kathryn Kimball Mizelle had sentenced Lamanna to 15 months in federal prison. The sentence followed her admission of guilt in the two offences.The DOJ's announcement also outlined the maximum penalties associated with the charges before sentencing. Embezzlement by a bank employee carried a potential maximum sentence of 30 years in prison, while making a false statement to a federal agency carried a potential maximum of 5 years.Special Assistant US Attorney Chris Poor prosecuted the case. The case shows how the theft of physical cash developed into a wider effort to manipulate financial records.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Best foods for reducing dangerous belly fat and protecting heart health
articles.summary: Belly fat and visceral fat are linked to serious health issues. A doctor shares how lean protein, fruits and vegetables, and healthy fats can help reduce stomach fat.
articles.body: Incorporating a few nutritious staples into the diet can help reduce belly fat and, in turn, lead to underlying health benefits. A surplus of fat around the stomach area can be an indication of visceral fat, which lies deep inside the abdomen and is linked to multiple health issues. Overweight individuals with excess fat around their midsections tend to be at greater risk for heart attacks and strokes, Dr. Michael Aziz, an internist based in New York City, told Fox News Digital. WANT TO DODGE THE FLU THIS YEAR? EAT THESE SECRET-WEAPON IMMUNITY-BOOSTING FOODS Genetics certainly contribute to obesity, Aziz acknowledged, but people can change their "genetic destiny" by making healthy choices such as eating a balanced diet and exercising regularly. Here are Aziz's recommendations for foods that can help beat belly fat and facilitate a healthier lifestyle. 1. Lean protein Sources of lean protein such as chicken breasts and eggs are low in calories but still satisfying. Some studies have shown that following high-protein diets can help burn extra calories, Aziz said, but consuming too much protein can increase the risk of kidney stones, heart attacks and strokes. articles.title: Two dead in Istanbul after heaviest rainfall in 84 years, governor says
articles.summary: Residents have been told to avoid leaving their homes unless absolutely necessary.
articles.body:
Two people have died after severe flooding caused by what the governor of Istanbul said was the heaviest rainfall in 84 years, BBC Turkish has reported.

A14-year-old boy died after he was electrocuted when he stepped in a puddle, while a 34-year-old man attempting to cross the road slipped and fell, hitting his head on the pavement.

Nearly 600 people have been rescued after becoming stranded, the city's deputy mayor said, with cars submerged in water in some districts.

Residents have been told by Istanbul Governor Davut Gül to avoid leaving their homes unless absolutely necessary.

The city's governorship is investigating the death of the teenaged boy who was electrocuted.

Some areas of Istanbul have seen rainfall equivalent to one seventh of the annual average, according to the interior minister. Schools were ordered to close on Thursday and Friday, as the rain is expected to continue.

Nuri Aslan, deputy mayor of the city, said 595 people had been evacuated to safe areas after becoming trapped, while more than 8,000 workers were responding to the flooding.

"I urge all our citizens to remain vigilant against the expected heavy rain and storm, particularly during nighttime hours," he wrote on X.

He told people to use public transport instead of private vehicles, with the city's metro hours expanded to 02:00 local time.

The flooding also impacted air travel, with 46 planes unable to land at airports in Istanbul, BBC Turkish said.

A car park in a shopping centre was flooded in the Sariyer district, with multiple vehicles submerged. Sections of roads in other areas collapsed, according to local media, and a river has burst its banks.

More than 16 million people live in the broader Istanbul metropolitan area. The interior ministry has also warned of sudden flooding in several provinces.

In response, employees who are disabled, pregnant or veterans will be granted administrative leave on Thursday, unless they work in health, safety, and rainwater drainage fields, Turkish media reported. Women working in the public sector who have children under the age of eight will also be granted leave.

articles.title: Toluwanisings: Nigerian gospel singer dies aged 41
articles.summary: His family has appealed to fans to remember his wife, children and family in prayer during this period of mourning.
articles.body:
One of Nigeria's most popular gospel singers, Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, known as Toluwanisings, has died, his family has announced.

In a statement posted on the deceased's Instagram page, the family said the singer had "said goodbye to the world" in the early hours of Wednesday, 14 October. He was 41.

They also appealed to fans to remember his wife, children and family in prayer during this period of mourning.

The family said burial arrangements would be announced in due course.

Toluwanisings was known for his beautiful voice and energetic praise performances that encouraged audience participation, according to some of the tributes paid by his fans on social media.

Some of his popular songs include Unreserved Praise, A Very Big God, Onibuore, E Lagbara and Owo Re Meji Meji.

There was panic among thousands of his fans on social media after news first emerged of his death on Wednesday before it was later confirmed by the family.

Toluwanisings' death comes months after he was involved in a road accident alongside members of his band.

Tributes have continued to pour in from colleagues and fans following the announcement of his death.

Among those who reacted are prominent lawyer Pelumi Olajengbesi and comedian Woli Agba, who had earlier called for prayers for the singer.

articles.title: Social Security's 2027 COLA is the biggest since 2023. How it affects your payments.
articles.summary: The payment increase reflects a year of high inflation and will benefit more than 72 million people.
articles.body:
Social Security and SSI benefits will increase by 3.6% in 2027 for more than 72 million people, the Social Security Administration (SSA) announced Wednesday.

The cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) is the biggest since 2023 and means, on average, retirement benefits will rise by $75 a month, SSA said.

The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB) says that works out to roughly $900 a year, and estimates the highest earners will see an increase of more than $2,200 a year.

SSA calculates the COLA based on the average year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (a form of measuring inflation) for July, August and September.

SSI recipients will see the first higher payment on Dec. 31, 2026. Some people receive both SSI and Social Security. Most Social Security recipients will be paid the higher amount starting Jan. 1, 2027.

The COLA will also affect Medicare Part B beneficiaries, whose premiums are deducted from their Social Security payments. The 2027 standard premium is projected to rise to $209.50 from $202.90, an increase of $6.60 a month, which would leave the average retired worker about $68 a month better off after COLA.

'Next year's COLA can't come soon enough'

SSA Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano said the adjustment will give beneficiaries "greater financial stability," and reflects a year of elevated inflation, particularly in gasoline and energy prices.

But Nancy Altman, president of the advocacy group Social Security Works, said the increase "doesn't fully account for the costs that Social Security beneficiaries face."

Altman said that's because the CPI-W, the inflation index used to calculate Social Security increases, tracks the costs of working people, not retirees, who she said spend a higher share of their income on health care and housing.

"Next year's COLA can't come soon enough for many Social Security beneficiaries," she told Yahoo.

The Senior Citizens League (TSCL), a nonpartisan seniors' group, was also critical of the payment increase. Executive director Shannon Benton said in a statement that the COLA "falls short of expectations" and that benefits lag behind price spikes because seniors don't see the adjustment until January.

It's a concern also shared by beneficiaries. AARP analysis released this week found that 76% of adults 50 and older said a COLA of around 3.5%, slightly lower than the announced figure, would not be enough to help them keep up with rising prices.

Kathleen Romig, director of Social Security and disability policy at the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, said the annual COLA increase is "especially important in times of high inflation."

"This year's COLA is bigger than in many recent years because of rising prices," she told Yahoo. "Another 3.6% … will help beneficiaries keep up with rising costs at the pump and in the grocery store."

"Gas and groceries can eat (COLA) up quickly, and that's before you factor in healthcare, where costs are projected to grow by an average of 5.4% a year over the next decade," Robert Laura, a retirement transition coach told Yahoo.

Some policy groups say the COLA calculation should be updated to use a measure that better reflects retirees' spending habits.

The Senior Citizens League wants COLA for retirees to be calculated based on a metric called the Consumer Price Index for the Elderly (CPI-E) .

Introduced by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) in 1987, it uses the same underlying price collection system as the main CPI, but instead calculates the market basket to reflect how older Americans actually spend their money , taking a snapshot of retirees' spending priorities as well as how much they spend out of pocket.

How do I check if I'm eligible for the increase?

You don't need to do anything. The increase is automatic for everyone receiving Social Security or SSI.

SSA said enrollees can see their 2027 Medicare Part B premium in their "my Social Security Message Center" starting in late November. Medicare changes will be posted at medicare.gov.

Beneficiaries will receive a simplified, one-page COLA notice with their new benefit amount, exact dates and any deductions.

Online: People with a personal my Social Security account can view the notice starting in late November, up to three weeks before a mailed notice. People without an account need to create one and enroll in paperless notices by Nov. 18 to see it online. Account holders can also sign up for text or email alerts.

By mail: Anyone not enrolled in paperless notices will get theirs in December.

For more information, see SSA's COLA page .

Nov. 18: Deadline to create a my Social Security account and enroll in paperless notices to see the notice online.

Late November: Online COLA notices will become available to paperless account holders, and Medicare enrollees can see their 2027 Part B premium in their Message Center. The premium is typically deducted directly from monthly Social Security payments.

Dec. 31, 2026 to January 2027: Beneficiaries begin receiving payments with the increase added.

SSI payments normally arrive on the first of the month, but the January payment will arrive on Dec. 31, 2026, because Jan. 1 is a federal holiday.

Social Security payments generally go out on the second, third or fourth Wednesday of the month, based on the beneficiary's birthday.

People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997, or who receive both Social Security and SSI, generally get their Social Security payment on the third of the month.

articles.title: Founded in 1889 by an English earl’s son, this Wyoming ranch stayed in the family for four generations; the 1,542-acre property, also visited by Queen Elizabeth II, hits the market for $24.5 million
articles.summary: This 1,542-acre Quarter Circle Lazy B Ranch in north-central Wyoming, which has been in one family since 1889, is now on the market.
articles.body: This 1,542-acre Quarter Circle Lazy B Ranch in north-central Wyoming, which has been in one family since 1889, is now on the market. The legacy property, which was once visited by Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, is listed for $24.5 million through Century 21 BHJ Realty.A legacy property owned by a family for four generationsTucked beneath the skyline of the Bighorn Mountains, this ranch was founded by Oliver H. Wallop (Noll), the youngest son of a Victorian earl. “He settled in southern Montana, where he introduced the region’s first thoroughbred horses. By 1889, he had moved south to Big Horn, Wyoming, establishing what became known as Canyon Ranch, which includes the historic Quarter Circle Lazy B,” the listing says.In 1925, he unexpectedly inherited the title of 8th Earl of Portsmouth. Despite his nobility, he remained devoted to his Wyoming ranch until his death in 1942. The land stayed with his descendants, and four generations of the Wallop family have owned it since. The family oversaw the property’s stewardship for 135 years.Oliver’s grandson, Malcolm Wallop, served for 18 years in the US Senate. His great-grandson, Paul Wallop, now owns the ranch and is its co-listing agent.Paul’s aunt married Henry Herbert, the 7th Earl of Carnarvon. Friends called him Porchie. He had known Queen Elizabeth II since childhood, and they shared a love of horses. In 1969, he became her horse-racing manager. Herbert’s family home is Highclere Castle in Hampshire, which later became the setting for the Netflix series Downton Abbey.Famous people visited the ranchIn 1984, Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip visited the ranch. They were in Kentucky looking at horses before travelling to Wyoming. They “had been looking at horses in Kentucky, and then they came out here,” Paul Wallop told Mansion Global. “They were here for four days. It was just a private family trip.” Philip had visited earlier, in 1969. Princess Anne also visited later.Among the famous visitors were the Japanese, Saudi and British ambassadors, former French President Valéry Giscard d’Estaing, former US Vice-President Dan Quayle and Hall of Famer John Elway, among others.What the buyer getsThis Wyoming ranch is the “Jewel on the face of the Bighorn Mountains”, according to the listing. And they are not wrong. The legacy property sits at the mouth of Little Goose Canyon, with the Bighorn Mountains close behind. The ranch is protected by one of Wyoming’s earliest conservation easements. “This land promises enduring tranquillity, privacy, and preservation,” the listing says. It is surrounded by other conserved ranches, and its vistas and open spaces remain untouched by development. The landscape, a “timeless Western setting”, unfolds across rolling pastures, lush meadows and pine forests, with panoramic mountain views.The main luxury lodge was built in 1993. It spans 3,006 square feet, with two bedrooms, a loft and four bathrooms. “The lodge is set in a wonderfully peaceful location just to the east of the main buildings and enjoys the full panoramic views of Little Goose Canyon and Moncrieffe Ridge,” according to the listing.The Foreman’s House dates to the early 1900s and was updated in 2011. The 1,444-square-foot house has three bedrooms and two bathrooms. There is also a cabin at the back of the ranch. It is “a comfortable 1¼-storey retreat with 1,377 square feet, two bedrooms, a sleeping loft and a bathroom”. There are also two barns, including a historic stone barn from the 1930s, and a riding arena measuring 100 by 200 feet. The old three-sided shop building is now used for storage.The land has four mountain ponds and 600 feet of trout stream. The ranch also holds one of Wyoming’s original private game bird farm licences.Three houses are used as holiday rentals, including a fly-fishing lodge and a remote cabin. That income is part of what the family has built around the property.Accessibility is another perk. The town of Sheridan is about 20 minutes away. Paul described its downtown as “thriving”, and most of Main Street is on the National Register of Historic Places. The area also has an old polo field which, according to the listing, is the oldest west of the Mississippi River.Nearby, Bear Davis Park and Red Grade Road provide access to Bighorn National Forest, which covers nearly one million acres of trails and wilderness. The local airport connects to Denver, where travellers can catch flights to most other destinations.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.
